# dsh-web-preview

在 DeepSeek Harness 右侧栏里直接预览网页，不用跳出 DSH 去开外部浏览器。

Preview web pages inside the DeepSeek Harness right sidebar — no external browser window needed.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-0.2.0--rc.1%2B-blue.svg)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![Topic: dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-0284c7.svg)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

> 装不上、报错、或者行为和文档对不上，直接发邮件到 **1992335297@qq.com**，比开 Issue 更快被看到。

---

![右侧栏网页预览](docs/preview.png)

> 图为界面示意，按插件 `lib/client.js` 的地址栏与 iframe 布局渲染，不是运行截图。可用 `node scripts/make-screenshots.mjs` 重新生成（源码在 `scripts/demo/preview.html`）。

## 它解决什么问题

写完前端要验证效果，标准流程是切到浏览器、开新标签、输地址、再切回来。真机上窗口一多就找不着北。DSH 的右侧栏本来就是文件预览的地盘，把网页也放进去，视线不用离开对话。

`dsh-web-preview` 给右侧栏加一个「网页预览」标签页：输入地址、回车，页面就在侧栏里跑起来。

## 用法

1. 点右侧栏 tab 条上的添加按钮，在引导页里选 **网页预览**。
2. 在地址栏输入 `localhost:5173` 或 `https://example.com`，回车。
3. 地址栏右侧三个按钮：重新加载、在外部浏览器打开、复制地址。

地址会自动补协议：`localhost:5173` 走 `http://`，裸域名走 `https://`。显式写了协议就按你写的来。

## 实现方式

走 DSH 官方的侧栏扩展点，不自绘面板、不覆盖既有 UI：

- 类型注册：`ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind, patterns, priority, title, guide })`
- 正文注册：`ctx.slots.register({ name: 'sidebar.right.pane.tab', key })`
- 导航：`ctx.sidebarRight.openResource('dsh-resource://web/<encodeURIComponent(url)>')`

每个预览地址是一个独立的资源 tab，同一地址重复打开会聚焦已有 tab，不会堆一堆重复页。tab 标题取目标站点的 host。

宿主侧只提供一个只读健康检查 `/api/web-preview/health`，不读文件、不落盘、没有对外网络请求。

## 安全边界

- iframe 只接受 `http` / `https`，其它协议直接拒绝。
- 拒绝把 DSH 自身的 origin 当作预览目标，避免把 DSH 页面嵌进自己造成同源脚本互扰。
- 不注入任何脚本到被预览的页面，不读取页面内容，不上报任何数据。
- 预览页运行在 iframe 的独立文档上下文里；父页面不获得它的 DOM。

## 已知限制

- 跨域页面无法被父页面读取 DOM，所以这一版只能「看」，不能「批注」。
- 拒绝承载体 X-Frame-Options / CSP `frame-ancestors` 的站点会白屏，这类站点请用地址栏右侧的 ↗ 打开到外部浏览器。
- 需要登录态的页面在侧栏里可能没有 cookie，取决于目标站点的 SameSite 策略。
- 尚未注册模型工具，目前由用户手动输入地址。

## 路线图

批注功能（指向页面元素、显示标签/尺寸/颜色/字体、点击就地下评论、批注回填输入框）二期实现。跨域 iframe 拿不到内部 DOM，二期改为宿主侧接管浏览器：Playwright 打开页面、CDP 推画面、坐标回传、`document.elementFromPoint` 取元素、注入批注覆盖层。

## 开发

```
lib/index.js         宿主侧：健康检查路由 + URL 规范化
lib/client.js        客户端侧：tab 类型注册、正文（地址栏 + iframe）
scripts/verify.mjs   自检
```

```bash
node scripts/verify.mjs
```

覆盖包元数据、patch 结构、客户端语法与依赖声明、同源防护、四类 URL 规范化用例、路由注册与健康检查、非法路由。共 14 项。

## 安装

### 一条命令

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:nubeslove/dsh-web-preview"
```

然后在 `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里追加 `"dsh-web-preview"`，重启 DSH。

实测 pnpm 11.9 从 GitHub 直接拉取，3.9 秒装完。插件是纯 JS，没有构建步骤，也没有任何运行时依赖。

### 本地开发

自己改代码时用 link 指向工作副本：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-web-preview"
```

路径含空格时手工处理：在 `profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dependencies` 加 `"dsh-web-preview": "link:E:/path/to/dsh-web-preview"`，在 `dsh.profile.bundles` 追加 `"dsh-web-preview"`，并在 `profiles/desktop/node_modules/` 下建指向本目录的 Junction，然后重启 DSH。

## 许可证

[MIT](LICENSE)

## 反馈与联系 / Feedback & Contact

遇到 bug、安装失败、行为和文档不一致，或者想要某个功能，都可以直接发邮件。

**邮箱：1992335297@qq.com**

邮件里带上这三样，定位会快很多：

- 插件版本（`package.json` 里的 `version`）
- DSH 版本（`dsh --version`）
- 报错的完整文字或截图

也可以在 [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/nubeslove/dsh-web-preview/issues) 提，但邮件更快。

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：上下文超过 45% 且静默 3 分钟时自动压缩会话历史
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-auto-compact

DeepSeek Harness 插件：**上下文占用超过 30%、且对话 3 分钟没有动静时，自动压缩会话历史。**

阈值、静默时长、巡检间隔、冷却时间都可配置。

> **EN** — A DSH host plugin that compacts a session automatically once its context
> usage passes a threshold (30% by default) **and** the conversation has been idle
> for a while (3 minutes by default). Zero runtime dependencies; it only decides
> *when*, and delegates the actual summarization to the official
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic` backend via `/compact`.

## 它解决什么问题

DSH 自带的自动压缩只在“回合进行中、跑到模型上下文阈值（默认 80%）”时才触发。
长会话往往在回合结束时停在 60%~80% 之间，之后你放着不动，下一句话照样要带着
一坨旧历史进请求：首 token 慢、贵，还容易在再聊几轮后直接顶到上限。

这个插件补上“空闲期”这一段：只要某个会话**已经静默够久**，且**上下文占用已过线**，
它就在后台把旧历史压成一条 checkpoint，等你回来时上下文是干净的。

## 判定规则

每个巡检周期（默认 15s）对每个存活会话依次检查：

| 条件 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.status === "idle"` | 回合正在跑时**绝不**介入，不和进行中的对话抢状态 |
| 静默 ≥ `idleMs` | 会话日志事件、agent 状态变化、收件箱投递都会刷新“最后活跃时间” |
| 上下文 ≥ `thresholdRatio` | 取 token-meter 的上下文投影（与界面显示的百分比同源） |
| 距离上次尝试 ≥ `cooldownMs` | 成功、失败、跳过都计入冷却，避免反复打扰模型 |
| 不在压缩中 | 单个会话同时只允许一次自动压缩 |

命中后调用官方压缩链路，把可压缩的历史压成一条 checkpoint。压缩本身产生的事件
会刷新活跃时间，所以不会连环触发。

## 安装

### 方式一：从 tgz 安装（推荐）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add file:C:/Plugins/dsh-auto-compact-0.1.0.tgz
```


### 方式二：从源码（GitHub）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fpm0312/dsh-auto-compact.git
cd dsh-auto-compact
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "file:$PWD/dsh-auto-compact-0.1.2.tgz"
```

PowerShell 里最后一行写成：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "file:$((Get-Location).Path)\dsh-auto-compact-0.1.2.tgz"
```

开发调试可以直接用 `link:` 挂目录（改动免重装，但需要重启应用让宿主重新 import）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "link:$PWD"
```

### 方式三：手工挂载（等价）

1. 把本包放进 profile 的依赖里（`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`）：
   `"dsh-auto-compact": "file:C:/Plugins/dsh-auto-compact-0.1.0.tgz"`
2. 在同一个文件的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里追加 `"dsh-auto-compact"`。
3. 在 profile 目录执行 `pnpm install`。

本包自带 `cordis.patch.yml`（`dsh.bundle.patch`），安装后会把 `auto-compact`
一行插进配置树，不需要手改 `cordis.patch.yml`。桌面端的 profile 监听会在
`package.json` / patch 变化时热重载插件树；否则重启一次应用即可。

## 配置

配置写在插件行上（profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`，或直接用上面的 `config` 段覆盖）：

```yaml
- id: auto-compact
  name: dsh-auto-compact
  config:
    thresholdRatio: 0.30     # 上下文占用阈值（占模型上下文窗口比例）
    idleMs: 180000           # 静默多久算“没动静”（毫秒）
    pollMs: 15000            # 巡检间隔（毫秒）
    cooldownMs: 300000       # 两次尝试之间的最小间隔（毫秒）
    minTokens: 0             # 低于这个绝对 token 数不压缩
    compactTimeoutMs: 600000 # 单次压缩超时
    dryRun: false            # true = 只记录“本该压缩”，不真的压
    statusFile: true         # 心跳状态文件；false 关闭，或给绝对路径
    via: auto                # auto | service | command
    verbose: true            # 是否输出 info 日志
```


### `via` 是什么

压缩后端挂在**每个 agent preset 的隔离作用域**里，宿主平面拿不到 `ctx.compaction`。
插件按以下顺序找通道：

1. `service`：`agent.ctx.get("compaction")` 能拿到就直接调 `compactNow()`；
2. `command`：拿不到就执行内置的 `/compact` 命令 —— 同一条官方压缩链路，
   会在会话日志里留下 `command/run` + `command/done`，界面上可见。

`auto`（默认）先试 1 再退 2；`service` / `command` 可以强制只走某一条。

## 可观测性

- **心跳文件**：默认 `~/.dsh/auto-compact.status.json`，每次巡检后刷新。里面有每个
  会话的 `totalTokens` / `contextWindow` / `ratio` / `reason` / `lastAction`，
  一眼能看出“为什么这次没压”。
- **命令**：`/autocompact` 查看当前会话的占用与判定；`/autocompact now` 立即评估一次
  （跳过静默等待，但仍受阈值与冷却约束）。
- **日志**：`[auto-compact]` 前缀，info 级汇报压缩结果，warn 级汇报真故障；
  “agent 忙 / 被取消”这类正常竞争只记 info。

## 设计取舍

- **只做决策，不重写压缩**：真正的摘要、写 checkpoint、替换 surface 全部交给
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic`，插件只负责“什么时候该压”。
- **零 `@deepseek-ai/*` 依赖**：安装成 tgz 后不需要解析宿主的 peer 依赖，宿主升级
  也不会因为类型/内部实现变化把插件带崩。
- **空闲优先**：绝不压缩正在跑的回合。压缩是重活（要调一次模型），空闲期做最划算。
- **百分比与界面同源**：优先读 token-meter 的 `contextPressure` 投影
  （`pressureTokens + surfaceTokens - sampledSurfaceTokens`），拿不到才退回
  `measure().totalTokens` 估算。

## 开发

```bash
node --test test/auto-compact.test.mjs   # 16 个用例：决策矩阵 + 假宿主集成
node --check lib/index.js
npm pack                                  # 产出 tgz
```


`test/` 里用假宿主驱动 `apply()`，覆盖：静默判定、阈值边界、运行中不介入、
事件刷新计时、冷却、dryRun、命令兜底、投影优先、心跳文件、`/autocompact`。

## 已知限制

- 只对**空闲**会话生效；回合进行中的压力压缩仍然交给 `compaction-basic` 自己的阈值
  （默认 80%）。两者互补，不冲突。
- 压缩会真实调用一次模型（摘要），会计费；`cooldownMs` 就是为此存在的。
- 如果 profile 里根本没有挂载任何压缩后端，`/compact` 也不存在，插件会如实报
  `missing` 并在心跳文件里留痕，不会静默失败。

plugins.description: Native Rapid-MLX provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — dsh reads model facts from the server instead of your settings.yaml.
plugins.readme_text:
# @raullenchai/dsh-provider

A native [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) provider for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — so `dsh`
gets its model facts from the server instead of from whatever you typed into
`settings.yaml`.

[![CI](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Status: published to npm** as
> [`@raullenchai/dsh-provider`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@raullenchai/dsh-provider).
> The end-to-end `dsh` run in [Verified](#verified) was on an M3 Ultra against
> `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`; `dsh 0.1.0-rc.8` is API-compatible — the `LlmAdapter`
> contract is byte-identical and the only changes are additive — and the
> adapter is re-verified against rc.8 at the protocol and unit-test level.
> DSH is still a developer preview that moves fast, so treat this as tracking
> a moving target, not a frozen compatibility promise.

## What it does for you

DSH can already talk to a local Rapid-MLX server through its generic
`openai-completions` provider. That route works — but it knows nothing about
your model beyond what you hand-wrote:

```yaml
# what the generic route makes you maintain, by hand, per model
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    rapid-mlx:
      baseURL: http://localhost:8000/v1
      defaultContextWindow: 262144      # you looked this up. is it still right?
      models:
        - id: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
          contextWindow: 262144
          reasoningEfforts: {off: none, low: low, medium: medium, high: high}
```

Rapid-MLX's `/v1/models` already publishes all of that and more. This adapter
reads it, so:

**1. Nothing to hand-write, and nothing to re-write when you switch models.**
Swap what `rapid-mlx serve` is running and `dsh` follows. No re-running setup,
no stale numbers.

**2. The reasoning control tells the truth.** Rapid-MLX reports whether a model
actually has a reasoning parser. A model that can't reason no longer shows an
off/low/medium/high selector that does nothing.

**3. Compaction is timed with the capacity that actually fits this Mac, not a
number that drifted.** This is the one that quietly costs you.
`dsh-compaction-basic` asks the provider for the route's capacity and compacts
at `thresholdRatio × capacity` (0.8 by default). The provider prefers the
server's **`max_model_len`** — Rapid-MLX's memory-fitted ceiling (what fits in
unified memory: weights + KV cache), in the vLLM/SGLang-standard field — over
the native `context_window`, and falls back to `context_window` on an older
server that doesn't report it. So compaction is timed to what the machine can
actually hold, not the model's advertised window (which it may not have room
for) and not a hand-written number copied from another model.

## Install

Needs Node ≥ 22.15 (dsh imports Node's Zstd stream API without declaring it)
and a running Rapid-MLX server.

```sh
# From npm:
dsh plugin --profile web add @raullenchai/dsh-provider

# …or straight from source — the package ships plain JS with no build step:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider

export RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1     # optional; this is the default
dsh web
```

Then point the agent at the route:

```yaml
# $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml
agent-default-model:
  provider: rapid-mlx
  model: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
```

Verified: that command installs and activates as a profile layer against
`dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`. To hack on it locally instead, see
[Local development](#local-development).

## Model management (v0.2.0)

Beyond the provider route, the plugin registers five tools and a `/rapid-mlx`
command so the agent can see and manage models without leaving the session.
The split follows which surface actually owns each fact: served-model facts
come from the structured HTTP `/v1/models`; the download cache and pull/remove
are CLI-only, so those — and only those — shell out to `rapid-mlx` through the
harness subprocess seam.

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rapid_mlx_serving` | HTTP `/v1/models` | The model(s) served right now, deduped, with context window, reasoning/tool parsers, MoE/hybrid, and modalities. |
| `rapid_mlx_cached` | `rapid-mlx models --cached` | Downloaded models and their on-disk size. |
| `rapid_mlx_pull` | `rapid-mlx pull <name>` | Download a model (alias or HF repo id). Cancellable; no fixed deadline. |
| `rapid_mlx_remove` | `rapid-mlx rm -y <name>` | Delete a cached model to free disk. |
| `rapid_mlx_health` | HTTP + `rapid-mlx --version` | API up? CLI reachable? Reported as two independent facts. |

`/rapid-mlx` prints a one-shot overview: health, the served model and its facts,
and total cache disk usage.

The CLI is resolved from the `cliCommand` config (default `rapid-mlx` on
`PATH`, or `$RAPID_MLX_CLI`); set it to an absolute path if the binary is not on
the harness's `PATH`. `rapid_mlx_pull`/`rapid_mlx_remove` are the only tools
that change anything on disk, and they run non-interactively (`rm` is forced
with `-y` because the subprocess seam ignores stdin).

## Verified

Against `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7` on an M3 Ultra:

- Installs and **activates as a profile layer** (no "declares no `dsh.bundle`"
  warning; the entry shows up in `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`).
- Registers the `rapid-mlx` route with `ctx.llm` and serves real queries.
- Plain chat, a single tool call, and the multi-step bug-fix task that gates
  Rapid-MLX releases — the last one fixed the bug and made the target repo's own
  test pass, verified independently, in 36 s on `qwen3.6-35b-8bit`.

## Not done yet

Being explicit, because the point of the adapter is to *use* what the server
says and some of it is still only read:

- `recommended_sampling` — should be applied automatically per model.
- `tool_call_parser` — should let `dsh` fail fast on a model that cannot emit
  `tool_calls`, instead of looping.
- `is_hybrid` / `is_moe` / `capabilities` — read, not yet acted on.
- **Memory-aware capacity.** Today `resolveModel()` reports the model's
  *advertised* context window. On a Mac the real ceiling is unified memory, and
  reporting that instead is the biggest remaining win — it needs Rapid-MLX to
  expose a usable-capacity figure first.
- Images are not carried through `stream()` — but they now **refuse** with
  `LlmError(..., 'UNSUPPORTED')` rather than being dropped, per the cookbook.
  Text, reasoning and tool calls are carried.
- The route is registered as `rapid-mlx`. If your `settings.yaml` also declares
  a `rapid-mlx` provider under `llm-pi-ai`, the two compete for one route name
  (`registerAdapter` owns provider exclusivity). Use one or rename ours.

## Conformance with the official adapter contract

Built against
[`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md)
and its "protocol obligations" section. Each item has a test:

| Obligation | How it is met |
|---|---|
| `usage` before `finish`, nothing after `finish` | usage is buffered and flushed at end-of-stream, so a trailing usage-only chunk cannot reorder it |
| Tool-call `arguments` are raw JSON strings end to end | fragments stream as `argumentsDelta` and reassemble unparsed |
| Block indexes in first-seen order, reused per block | verified across a reasoning-then-text response |
| Errors take exactly two sanctioned paths | transport/protocol failures **throw** `LlmError` with a stable code; nothing ends the stream quietly |
| Honor `options.signal` | passed to `fetch` and to the SSE reader; an `AbortError` is re-thrown unchanged, not reclassified |
| A field the provider cannot honor throws `UNSUPPORTED` | image content refuses instead of being narrowed away |
| Config is a schemastery schema with env fallback | `export const Config`, fed from `cordis.patch.yml` via `!!js process.env.RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL` |

`finish.replayState` is not emitted: Rapid-MLX needs no native response ids
or signatures on follow-up calls, so there is nothing lossless to project.

plugins.description: Switch DSH's built-in web_search between the DeepSeek Search API (/v1/tools/search) and the default account search, with live fallback, a settings page and a sidebar switch.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-deepsearch

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-deepsearch)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-deepsearch)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/github-SeaViod%2Fdsh--plugin--deepsearch-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/SeaViod/dsh-plugin-deepsearch)

Switch DSH's built-in `web_search` between the **DeepSeek Search API** (`POST /v1/tools/search`) and DSH's default account search — with automatic fallback, a settings page, a sidebar switch and a model-facing tool.

English | [中文说明](README.zh.md)

- **ON (`deepseek-api`)** — the built-in `web_search` tool is served by the DeepSeek Search API. This is a paid API: successful requests are billed by DeepSeek; check the current pricing in your DeepSeek console before enabling it.
- **OFF (`builtin`)** — the default DSH route: server-side account search (one search consumes one model turn).
- Switching is **immediate** and survives restarts: the mode is persisted in `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-mode.json`.
- **It never makes search unavailable.** With no key, a 401, a network error, or 429/5xx retries exhausted, the provider falls back to the previous (or another available) search provider and reports the reason in `lastError`.
- **Zero runtime dependencies** — only `node:` builtins and the global `fetch`. No build step.
- Settings page and sidebar switch are localized in **English and Chinese**.

## What it does

The plugin has two halves that work together:

| Half | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `index.js` | Registers the model tool `deepsearch`, registers a search provider (default id `deepseek-search-api`), routes `web.searchProviderId` on/off, exposes four HTTP routes under `/deepsearch/`, and resolves the API key. |
| Browser | `client.js` | Hand-written bundle loaded through `window.__ModuleLoader__.load(...)`: the settings tab and the sidebar footer switch. |

`cordis.patch.yml` is the bundle patch: a `dsh plugin add` or plugin-market install puts the package into the profile's `node_modules` (recorded in the profile `package.json` under `dsh.profile.bundles`), and the bundle layer applies this patch at boot — you do not need to edit the profile patch by hand.

## Three entry points

| Entry point | Where | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Settings page | **Settings → Built-in plugins → DeepSeek Search** | switch, status details, endpoint test, API key editor |
| Sidebar switch | Footer of the left sidebar | one-click toggle that shows the current route (`API` / `builtin`) |
| Model tool | `deepsearch` (`status` / `on` / `off` / `search` / `fetch` / `check`) | toggle the route or run a search from a conversation |

## Install

### From the plugin market

Search for **dsh-plugin-deepsearch** (or "DeepSeek Search") in the DSH plugin market and install it. The storefront uses the package's `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the host half is registered automatically. After installing, the new settings tab appears under **Settings → Built-in plugins → DeepSeek Search**; a browser page reload may be needed the first time so the client bundle is picked up.

### From the command line

```pwsh
# Install into the default profile
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-deepsearch

# Or target a profile explicitly: `web` for a `dsh web` server
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-deepsearch
```

Installing for the **Desktop app** uses the desktop profile / the in-app plugin market UI (the Desktop app keeps its profile under its own DSH home; no user-home path has to be typed by hand). The plugin's browser half declares `dsh.client.platform: "web"`, which is what the desktop shell also loads.

If you are installing from a checkout rather than the registry, `npm pack` the folder and `dsh plugin add` the resulting tarball.

### Upgrading from 0.1.x

0.1.x had no bundle patch; it was installed by hand with one insert row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: deepsearch
      name: dsh-plugin-deepsearch
```

0.2.0 ships `dsh.bundle.patch` (`cordis.patch.yml` at the package root). A `dsh plugin add` or plugin-market install does **not** write an insert row into the profile patch: it installs the package into the profile's `node_modules`, records it in the profile's `package.json` under `dsh.profile.bundles`, and the bundle layer applies the package's own `cordis.patch.yml` at boot. **Remove the old hand-written insert row before installing 0.2.0 as a bundle** — a leftover hand-written row plus a bundle install would load the plugin twice. Mode and key files under `$DSH_HOME` are kept, so the switch state and the key file survive the upgrade.

The profile name depends on the client: use `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-deepsearch` for a `dsh web` server; the Desktop app uses the `desktop` profile and its plugin-market UI. Do not type a full profile path — let `dsh plugin` resolve it.

### Uninstall

Remove the package from the profile (or uninstall it from the plugin market). The plugin does not add other files to the profile. The state file `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-mode.json`, the diagnostics file `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-diag.json` and the optional key file `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-key.txt` can be deleted, or left in place if you plan to reinstall.

## Configuration

Configuration is read from the `config` block of the plugin's entry in the profile patch, and is normalized so that invalid values fall back to the defaults instead of throwing:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: deepsearch
      name: dsh-plugin-deepsearch
      config:
        apiKeyEnv: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
        count: 8
        retryCount: 1
```

All keys are optional. The table below matches the host config schema; the `config` block is also what a bundle install can carry.

| Key | Default | Normalisation / meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | `''` | API key given inline. String, trimmed; empty means "unset". Not recommended: it stays in the patch file. Never echoed back by any route. |
| `apiKeyEnv` | `'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'` | Name of the credentials reference / environment variable to resolve. Must match `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`, otherwise the default is used. |
| `baseURL` | `'https://api.deepseek.com'` | API base URL. Trimmed; must parse as an `http(s)` URL; trailing slashes are stripped. |
| `searchPath` | `'/v1/tools/search'` | Search endpoint path (appended to `baseURL`). Trimmed, forced to start with `/`; a `?` or `#` rejects the value; empty falls back to the default. |
| `fetchPath` | `'/v1/tools/fetch'` | Page-fetch endpoint path (same rules as `searchPath`). |
| `keyFile` | `''` | Key file for the file-based key. `''` means `$DSH_HOME/deepsearch-key.txt`; `~/...` expands to the home directory; a relative path resolves under `$DSH_HOME`; anything else is used as an absolute path. |
| `count` | `8` | Number of search results. Integer, clamped to 1..50. |
| `needContent` | `false` | Ask the search API for page content (direct `deepsearch search` calls only). Only a strict `true` enables it. |
| `timeoutMs` | `30000` | Timeout per HTTP attempt. Integer, clamped to 1000..120000. |
| `retryCount` | `1` | Extra attempts after the first one (on 408/429/5xx). Integer, clamped to 0..3. |
| `retryDelayMs` | `1200` | Delay between retry attempts. Integer, clamped to 100..10000. |
| `maxFetchChars` | `20000` | Maximum characters returned by `fetch`/the `search` tool when content is requested. Integer, clamped to 1000..200000. |
| `providerId` | `'deepseek-search-api'` | Search provider id to register. Must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/` and must not collide with an existing provider, except for the plugin's own re-registration. |
| `fallbackProvider` | `''` | Preferred fallback provider id used when switching OFF. Empty means auto-detect (the previously active provider, then the first available provider that is not ours). |
| `fallbackOnError` | `true` | When the Search API call fails, fall back to another provider. Only a strict `true` enables it. |
| `language` | `'auto'` | `auto` / `en` / `zh`. `auto` resolves from `DSH_LANGUAGE`, `DSH_LOCALE`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL` (Chinese locales map to `zh`, everything else to `en`). |
| `checkQuery` | `'DeepSeek'` | Query used by the "tes

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

Engramory is a **portable memory *discipline*, not a

plugins.description: Peak and off-peak pricing awareness for DeepSeek Harness: a live composer badge with the time left in the current window, converted to your timezone. Community plugin, not official.
plugins.readme_text:
**DeepSeek charges half price outside peak hours. This tells you when that is.** COMMUNITY PLUGIN  ·  NOT OFFICIAL  ·  MIT  ·  DSH 0.2.x

[Install](#install)  ·  [Use](#use)  ·  [How it works](#how-it-works)  ·  [Timezones](#timezones)  ·  [FAQ](#faq)

> **This is a community plugin, not an official DeepSeek product.** > > Peak Hours is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, > or supported by DeepSeek AI, and it is not part of DeepSeek Harness. DeepSeek > Harness and DeepSeek are names and marks of their respective owners. ## Why this exists DeepSeek's API has two prices. Off-peak costs half of the peak rate. The windows are written in UTC, on a Beijing calendar, in a paragraph on the pricing page. That is the correct way to define the policy and a terrible way to read it from Tel Aviv at 17:35. You do the arithmetic in your head, guess, or notice the difference on the invoice later. Peak Hours puts one badge in the composer bar. It says **Peak** or **Off-peak** and how long the current window has left. Click it and you get the day as a clock face, the schedule in your own timezone, and the exact moment the price changes. | | Peak | Off-peak | | --- | --- | --- | | Rate | full price | **half price** | | UTC | 01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00 | every other hour | | Beijing | 09:00–12:00, 14:00–18:00 | nights, weekends, holidays | | Days | Monday to Friday, not a Chinese public holiday | weekends and holidays, all day | The plugin answers one question: which column am I in, and for how much longer. ## What it looks like

Light and dark. The 24-hour face is your local day, with every peak window in amber and a marker for now.

The badge is small enough to ignore while you type. The ring drains over the current window, so a glance tells you whether you have minutes or hours. | | Off-peak | Peak | | --- | --- | --- | | Badge accent | green | amber | | Ring | drains over the off-peak stretch | drains over the peak window | | Panel chip | half rate | peak rate | ## Install **Requires [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 0.2.x** (tested on `0.2.1-rc.1`). Desktop and the Web UI are both supported. The repository is the install unit. The package inside it is `dsh-peak-hours`; the spec you paste is the GitHub address. ### 1. From the Plugins page (recommended) 1. Open the sidebar and choose **Plugins**. 2. Install a plugin and paste: ```text github:Adolanium/dsh-peak-hours ``` 3. Install it. The bundle is enabled by default. 4. Refresh the DeepSeek Harness window (`Ctrl+R` / `Cmd+R`). The browser half loads lazily, so the badge appears after a reload. No build permission is needed. The package ships plain JavaScript, has no `prepare` script, and has no runtime dependencies. ### 2. With the `dsh` CLI ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Adolanium/dsh-peak-hours ``` `dsh` appends the bundle to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` because the package declares `dsh.bundle`. Start DeepSeek Harness afterwards, then refresh the window. Pin the install to this release: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Adolanium/dsh-peak-hours#v0.1.0 ``` Remove it with: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-peak-hours ``` ### 3. From a checkout (development) ```sh git clone https://github.com/Adolanium/dsh-peak-hours.git cd dsh-peak-hours ./scripts/install-dev.sh ``` That links the checkout into `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules` and adds the plugin's Loader entry to the profile patch, with a timestamped backup. Undo it with `./scripts/uninstall-dev.sh`. > The profile reloads configuration live, so the Host half activates without a > restart. The browser half is loaded lazily: refresh the window for code > changes. ## Use Open any session. The badge sits in the composer bar, just left of the model selector. **The badge** shows the current window and the time left. It recalculates every second, so it never drifts. **The panel** opens on click: - the countdown, to the second; - a 24-hour face of your local day, with peak windows in amber and a marker for now; - the next change, for example `Peak starts today at 09:00`; - the full schedule converted into your timezone, and the reason for today (`Weekday`, `Weekend`, or a holiday name); - your timezone with its current offset, and the same moment in Beijing. `Esc` or a click outside closes it. The badge keeps ticking while the panel is closed. Below one hour the panel counts seconds. Above one hour it counts minutes, which is what you want when the answer is "two days". ## How it works ```text your clock │ ├─ Beijing calendar: weekday? public holiday? ├─ UTC windows: 01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00 ▼ countdown + local-day arcs ``` Three rules keep it honest: 1. **The policy is evaluated where it is written.** Peak windows are UTC instants. Whether a day is a peak day is a Beijing calendar question, so the plugin asks the Beijing calendar, not your `Date` object. A Friday 23:00 in Los Angeles is a Saturday in Beijing, and the badge says so. 2. **The rendering is yours.** Those instants are formatted with `Intl` in your own zone. Daylight saving time is handled by the platform, not by fixed offsets, and a 23 or 25 hour local day still draws correctly on the face. 3. **No zone, no pretending.** If the runtime cannot resolve a timezone, the plugin falls back to Beijing time and labels the panel `Beijing time · fallback`. It never presents a guess as your local time. The badge is one registration in `conversation.input.right`. It uses the Harness theme tokens for every surface and text color, so it follows your theme, including custom ones. There is no Host route, no network request, and no state written to disk. ## Timezones Peak windows are the same instants everywhere. The clock times are not: | Your zone | Peak hours, local time | | --- | --- | | Beijing (UTC+8) | 09:00–12:00 · 14:00–18:00 | | Jerusalem (UTC+3) | 04:00–07:00 · 09:00–13:00 | | Kolkata (UTC+5:30) | 06:30–09:30 · 11:30–15:30 | | Los Angeles (UTC-7) | 18:00–21:00 · 23:00–03:00 | The second Los Angeles window crosses local midnight. The panel prints it as `23:00–03:00` and the day face shows the part that falls inside today, because that is what your clock does. The timezone comes from the operating system or browser. It is read when the badge appears, so after a flight or a manual timezone change, refresh the window. ## The holiday calendar Chinese public holidays are off-peak all day. The plugin ships the official 2026 schedule from [国办发明电〔2025〕7号](https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12406/202511/content_7048922.html): | Holiday | Dates | | --- | --- | | New Year's Day | 1 to 3 January | | Spring Festival | 15 to 23 February | | Qingming | 4 to 6 April | | Labour Day | 1 to 5 May | | Dragon Boat | 19 to 21 June | | Mid-Autumn | 25 to 27 September | | National Day | 1 to 7 October | China designates 14 February, 28 February, 9 May, 20 September, and 10 October in 2026 as make-up workdays. They fall on a Saturday or Sunday, so the Monday to Friday policy leaves them off-peak. The plugin does not treat them as working days. The State Council publishes the next year's schedule each November. When it does, add the spans to `HOLIDAYS` in [`lib/client.js`](lib/client.js) and update the count in the test. Until then, a date outside the table follows the weekday rule. ## What it does not do - It does not change what you pay or which model you use. - It does not call the DeepSeek API, and it does not store your usage. - It does not add a rou

plugins.description: AI 错题本：把扫描试卷整理成以知识点为索引的错题合集（dsh-plugin）
plugins.readme_text:
# AI 错题本 · DSH 插件

把**扫描试卷**变成一本**以知识点为索引的错题本**：投喂 PDF/图片 → 插件建批次并光栅化 → 模型在会话里读卷面、提取错题 → 生成卡片草稿 → **你确认后**归档进 `library/`，并自动重建索引。

不是"AI 帮你解题"，而是"AI 帮你把卷面上**已经存在**的东西整理成可复习的结构"。

## 功能

- **扫描件直读**：PDF 自动光栅化（默认 400 dpi），切成整页概览 + 高清横带；看不清时按需索取原生分辨率重切
- **只在错题上花力气**：按你报的题号逐题提取，题干、作答、划改、页边演算、卷面标注、知识点、错因、难度
- **绝不编造**：读不准的内容写进"待人工确认"，交给人核对
- **卡片即 Markdown**：`library/<学科>/<卷子>/cards/*.md`，带 front-matter，可手改、可 diff、可进版本库
- **知识点索引**：自动重建 `index.md` / `index.json`，按 学科 → 一级 → 二级知识点 归类
- **导出打印版 PDF**：每道错题的板块可勾选；**公式以 Word 原生公式（OMML）排版**，不是 Unicode 拼凑
- **回收站**：删除先进 `_trash/`，可逐项还原，清空才真正销毁
- **会话可追溯**：待归档页可跳回分析会话继续修改

## 环境要求

- **DSH（DeepSeek Harness）桌面版**，Web/桌面 profile 均可。要求 DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.2`
- 分析模型需要**支持图片输入**（插件启动前会校验，不支持会直接报错而不是静默失败）
- Node.js ≥ 22（DSH 自带运行时已满足）

## 安装

### 方式一：从 npm 安装（最快，推荐）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ai-mistake-book
```

### 方式二：从 GitHub 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:suanmingxing/dsh-ai-mistake-book
```

> 把 `desktop` 换成你实际使用的 profile（桌面版通常是 `desktop`，`dsh web` 用 `web`）。
> 装完**重启 DeepSeek Harness** 生效。

### 方式三：本地目录（开发/调试）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/suanmingxing/dsh-ai-mistake-book.git D:\tools\dsh-ai-mistake-book
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "link:D:/tools/dsh-ai-mistake-book"
```

> `link:` 安装时 pnpm 不会替插件装 `dependencies`，所以本仓库**已把必要依赖放在 `node_modules/` 里一并提交**（见 [VENDOR.md](VENDOR.md)）。若你删掉了它，请手动补装：`npm i @deepseek-ai/schemastery @deepseek-ai/cosmokit katex`。

## 首次使用

1. **设置归档根**：设置 → 插件 → AI 错题本 → `archiveRoot`，填一个你希望存放错题本的绝对路径（默认 `~/.dsh/ai-mistake-book`）。改这个字段需要重启插件。
2. **建一个"归档工作区"会话**：在 DSH 里打开该目录作为工作区（首次 `/mistake` 会自动创建）。
3. **投喂试卷**：
   ```
   /mistake 错题为 3、5、6、8、9、11 题  @"C:\path\to\扫描卷.pdf"
   ```
   或在插件页用模型工具 `mistake_ingest` 指定文件路径。
4. **等分析**：分析在当前会话里进行；期间该会话的工具会被临时收窄到 4 个（读页面、提交候选、提交决定、问用户确认），结束后自动恢复。
5. **确认归档**：插件页 →「待归档」核对候选 →「管理」里导出 PDF 或删除；正式归档需在插件页确认。

## 数据与隐私

- **所有数据都在你自己的机器上**：试卷、转录、卡片、导出件都在 `archiveRoot` 下，插件不向任何第三方服务上传内容
- 模型调用走你 DSH 里配置的 provider（同样的调用链路，不会额外外发）
- 归档根结构：

```
<archiveRoot>/
├─ inbox/<batchId>/     进行中的批次（原始扫描、光栅图）
├─ library/<学科>/<卷子>/cards/*.md   归档后的错题卡片
├─ templates/           可编辑的提示词模板（analysis / background / error-taxonomy）
├─ exports/             导出的 PDF
├─ _trash/              回收站
└─ index.md / index.json  自动生成的索引
```

## 主要设置项

| 设置 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `archiveRoot` | `~/.dsh/ai-mistake-book` | 错题本存放位置 |
| `pdfDpi` / `overviewDpi` | 400 / 200 | 横带与整页概览的分辨率 |
| `pagesPerRequest` | 2 | 一次投喂几页（每页 1 概览 + N 横带） |
| `maxRecutsPerPage` | 4 | 每页原生重切配额 |
| `restrictAnalysisTools` | true | 分析期间收窄会话工具集 |
| `analysisProvider` / `analysisModel` | 空 | 空 = 用部署默认；必须支持图片 |
| `deleteToTrash` | true | 删除进回收站而非销毁 |

## 自定义提示词

设置页可编辑三份内置模板（`templates/`），也可以新增**自定义模板**：每条有标题、说明、正文，启用后自动并入分析任务书的「用户自定义要求」一节。

## 依赖说明

本插件在 `node_modules/` 里**随包提交**了三份依赖（合计约 0.7 MB）：`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`、`@deepseek-ai/cosmokit`（DSH 发布版，公开 npm 同版本）、`katex`。原因与升级方式见 [VENDOR.md](VENDOR.md)。

`katex` 仅用于会话内的公式预览（MathML），缺失时会降级为纯文本，不影响归档。

## 已知限制

- 公式排版覆盖错题卡常见写法（分数、根式、上下标、向量、`\left…\right`、希腊字母与常用运算符）；矩阵、分段函数等结构暂不支持，会退化为可读文本
- 分析依赖模型的视觉能力；看不清的字段会进入"待人工确认"，不会猜测
- 仅支持中文界面（`locale/` 目前只有 meta）

## 许可证

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 suanmingxing

plugins.description: DSH 模型故障自动转移 · provider-pool failover: on rate limit/quota/timeout, auto-retry with the next untried model from the selected providers' full model pools. Runtime tool: model_failover.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-model-failover — 模型故障自动转移

> DeepSeek Harness 插件：模型请求失败时，自动切换到「所选供应商池」中的下一个模型重试。

## 它解决什么

DSH 官方模型选择是「一次选定、失败就报错」。官方 `dsh-llm-retry` 只在**同一供应商**内重试——
如果供应商整体限流/配额耗尽/宕掉，重试 5 次后这一轮仍然失败。

本插件在**供应商之间**做故障转移：

- **池 = 所选供应商下的全部模型**：只选一个供应商 → 该供应商内所有模型轮询；选多个 → 按顺序跨供应商池轮询。
- **失败即切**：`RATE_LIMIT` / `QUOTA` / `TIMEOUT` / `SERVER` / `TRANSPORT` / `EMPTY_RESPONSE` 等
  可配置的机器可路由 code 触发；每个候选模型只试一次，绝不重复试同一个。
- **池尽即还原**：整个池都失败时交还原错误，不掩盖真实故障。
- **运行时可控**：`model_failover` 工具随时 `status / set / clear / enable / disable`，不用改配置重启。
- **可粘滞**：`sticky: true` 时转移后该会话持续使用新模型；默认只转移当次故障。

## 机制（与 DSH 官方扩展点对齐）

1. `agent/request-error` 瀑布流（官方重试插件同款扩展点）：上游 `dsh-llm-retry` 同供应商重试耗尽后
   返回 `undefined`，本插件接住失败 → 从池中挑下一个未试过的模型 → 返回 `{ kind: "retry" }`，
   agent-loop 重新 `prepareRequest` 并重发。
2. `agent/request` 瀑布流：把待生效目标写进本次请求的 provider/model，成为实际发送的模型
   （与 dsh-session-conductor 的成员模型切换同一模式）。
3. 失败分类只认 `failure.code`（机器可路由），绝不解析报错文本。
4. 状态存 `<DSH_HOME>/model-failover/state.json`：运行时池、粘滞目标、modelCatalog 快照、最近事件。
   不写会话事件（Session 拒绝未知 type 的非 ignorable 事件）。

## 安装

本仓库是一个 Host-only bundle（无第三方依赖、无需构建）：

```
dsh-model-failover/
├── index.js            # 宿主插件主体
├── cordis.patch.yml    # bundle patch（insert 一行）
├── package.json        # dsh.bundle.patch 声明
├── locale/{en,zh}.json # 插件市场显示名/描述
└── icon.svg
```

通过 DSH 的 Plugin Manager 安装该目录（`install_bundle`，target 传本目录绝对路径），
或把目录放进 profile 的 `node_modules/` 并在 `cordis.patch.yml` 追加：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-model-failover
      name: dsh-model-failover
      config: {}
```

重启 DSH 生效。

## 配置（cordis.patch.yml 行 config，全部有默认值）

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | 总开关 |
| `providers` | `[]` | 默认供应商池（按顺序）；空 = 用 `model_failover set` 运行时设置 |
| `retryableCodes` | `RATE_LIMIT, QUOTA, ACCOUNT_QUOTA, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT, EMPTY_RESPONSE, NO_ADAPTER` | 触发转移的失败码 |
| `sticky` | `false` | 转移后粘滞该会话直到 `clear`；false = 仅当次故障内转移 |
| `maxFailoverAttempts` | `0` | 单次故障最多转移几个候选（0 = 整个池子） |

## 运行时工具 `model_failover`

| action | 参数 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | — | 查看开关/池（含候选模型列表）/触发码/最近 8 条转移事件 |
| `set` | `providers: ["wb","agnes"]` | 设置运行时池（优先于 config.providers），立即生效 |
| `clear` | — | 清空运行时池与粘滞目标，回退配置池 |
| `enable` / `disable` | — | 运行时总闸 |

示例：

```text
model_failover set providers=["wb","agnes"]   → 池 = wb 全部模型 + agnes 全部模型（按此顺序）
model_failover status                          → 池 6 个候选：wb/cn:a, wb/cn:b, … agnes/global:x
```

## 图形界面（输入框右下角）

插件自带浏览器半边：在输入框右下角、官方「模型选择器」左侧有一个 **⇄ 故障转移** 按钮，
点开后可以：

- 勾选一个或多个供应商（池 = 所选供应商内的全部模型，实时显示每个供应商的模型数）
- 保存 / 清空 / 停用·启用，点一下立即生效（与 `model_failover` 工具共用同一份状态）
- 查看当前池大小与最近几次转移事件

数据与操作走宿主同源路由 `GET /api/model-failover/status`、`POST /api/model-failover/{set,clear,toggle}`。
新增/修改 Client 代码后需要重启 DSH 并刷新页面（桌面端不做热加载）。

## 与其它插件的协同

- **dsh-llm-retry（官方）**：天然协同——上游先同供应商重试（自带退避），耗尽后本插件接住做跨供应商转移。
- **dsh-session-conductor（成员模型切换）**：两者都在 `agent/request` 改写模型。本插件在有待生效转移目标
  或 sticky 粘滞时生效；显式成员模型不会被无故障时改写（无 pending 时不干预）。

## 已知边界

- 池成员来自 `modelCatalog`；目录不可用时用最近的落盘快照（重启后仍可用）。
- 图片消息 + 纯文本模型：本插件不检查候选模型的输入模态（v1），如池内含纯文本模型可能在该轮被拒。
- 转移发生在同一步内，可能增加该步耗时（每个候选一次完整请求尝试 + 官方退避）。
- 不做「定时轮询」：只有失败才转移（按设计）。

## 测试

```bash
node --test test/unit.mjs
```

覆盖：池展开（单/多供应商、去重、未知跳过）、失败码过滤、路由改写、全链路
（失败 → 转移 → 重试 → 池尽还原）、运行时 set 立即生效、sticky/非 sticky 行为、状态持久化 + 快照兜底。

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Live wallpaper layer for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — procedural presets, images, GIF and video behind a translucent shell
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lively

Live wallpaper layer for the **DeepSeek Harness Web GUI**: an animated wallpaper
behind the interface — procedural presets, images, GIF or video — with a small
settings page to pick the look.

![Light theme preview](docs/preview-light.png)

## Features

- **Five procedural presets** — Aurora, Starfield, Lava, Mesh, Neon grid. Each
  has a dark variant for the dark palette and a bright variant for the light
  palette, so a light theme never ends up with a grey wash.
- **Custom wallpaper** — image, GIF, WebP, AVIF, MP4 or WebM, by URL or uploaded
  from disk. Uploads live under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-lively-media/` and are served by
  the plugin's own route, so they survive a reload and a restart.
- **Controls** — wallpaper strength (how much wallpaper shows through), dim,
  video softness, animation speed, pause when the window is hidden.
- **Theme aware** — the veil is keyed on `body[data-ds-dark-theme]`; the
  bright/dark preset variants are keyed on `html[data-dsh-lively-tone]`.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hero-jianghaojie/dsh-lively.git
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-lively
```

Then restart DSH (the sidebar's restart button, if installed) and open
**Settings → Live wallpaper**.

## How it works

- The wallpaper is the **root element's background** (`html`), i.e. the canvas —
  the one surface always below every column. Only video needs a real element, so
  a fixed `z-index:-1` layer exists solely for that case.
- The shell paints `--dsw-alias-bg-base` on the frame *and* on the centre
  column, and alphas multiply. The token is therefore fully **transparent**, and
  the single theme-coloured veil is drawn once on the canvas pseudo-elements
  (`html::before` for the veil, `html::after` for the dim).
- No `backdrop-filter` on the shell columns: it would make them the containing
  block for fixed-position descendants, and the sidebar's fold toggle is
  `position: fixed` — frosting the column drags that button onto the brand mark.
- Settings persist twice: `localStorage` (instant) and
  `$DSH_HOME/dsh-lively-state.json` via `/dsh-lively/state`, because the Desktop
  app's loopback port changes on every launch.

## Limitations

- A video wallpaper needs a real `<video>` element; CSS alone cannot play video.
- The softness control applies to video only — CSS cannot blur the root
  background, and blurring the columns breaks fixed-position shell chrome.
- The frame-transparency rule targets `[class$='_frame']`, which follows the
  shell's CSS-module naming.

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Curated durable memory for DeepSeek Harness: automatic capture, progressive-disclosure recall, duplicate folding and conflict resolution, plus a sidebar management panel.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-memory-curator

Curated durable memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh): automatic
capture of decisions, corrections, prohibitions and open work; progressive-disclosure recall;
duplicate consolidation; and old-vs-new conflict resolution. Everything is local — one JSON
store under `$DSH_HOME`, no network of its own, no account, no API key. Model calls reuse the
Harness `llm` service, so memory inherits the user's provider, credentials and retry policy.

[中文说明](#中文说明)

## Install

A plain Cordis bundle: no build step, no runtime dependencies.

```bash
# 1. install it into the profile that runs your DSH
cd "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/desktop"    # your own profile directory
pnpm add link:/path/to/dsh-memory-curator

# 2. list it as a bundle in that profile's package.json, e.g.
#    "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [
#      "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-memory-curator" ] } }
```

Restart DSH. The host half mounts capture, recall, curation and the six `memory_*`
tools; the browser half adds the **Memory** entry to the left sidebar. The package ships
`cordis.patch.yml` — the patch DSH applies while composing the tree — so the plugin row
and its default configuration come from the package itself.

DSH's plugin manager (Settings → Plugins) accepts the same `link:` spec and performs both
steps for you; a page refresh is enough after that, no rebuild.

## What it does

| | Behaviour | How |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Auto-capture** | When a turn ends, the conversation is distilled into durable entries worth keeping across sessions: designated technical references, architecture decisions, explicit corrections, prohibitions, and unfinished work. | A fire-and-forget listener on `session/event` (`turn/end`) sends the new messages to one bounded auxiliary LLM call; the validated candidates are persisted. Memory work can never delay or fail a turn. |
| **B. Progressive recall** | Each turn gets a bounded one-line-per-entry index: the entries that change behaviour (decisions, corrections, prohibitions, open work) come first, then the most recent facts. Full text is fetched only on demand. | A resident catalog is injected into the system prompt (tier 0). `memory_search` returns short digests with ids (tier 1). `memory_detail` returns the complete entry (tier 2) and records the read, which feeds the ordering and the decay pass. The standing prompt cost stays flat as the store grows. |
| **C. Curation** | Duplicate knowledge folds into one entry; a newer decision on the same subject retires the outdated one. | A deterministic pass runs on every insert and periodically: same-subject decisional entries conflict, the newer wins, the older is kept as history with a `supersededBy` pointer. A model-assisted pass adjudicates the similar-subject pairs the deterministic pass cannot settle, biased toward `coexist` so a true memory is never wrongly retired. |

## What memory does not record

The plugin deliberately does not overlap with the artifacts a project already keeps. Any one
of these tests means *record nothing*:

| Test | Where that information belongs instead |
|---|---|
| Would a future session get it from the repository? Architecture, file paths, build and test commands, dependency lists, directory layout, git history. | The code and git themselves. |
| Is it a project-level instruction — a convention, an "always/never" rule? | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, where every teammate and every tool sees it. Memory is machine-local and invisible to the rest of the team. |
| Is it task state — progress, next steps, a worked-off plan? | `STATE.md`, a todo list, or the issue tracker. |
| Is it a report that something was just done? "published the repository", "rewrote the history", "added a section". | The artifact is its own record. |

To make the first two decidable rather than a matter of taste, every distillation call carries
the repository context: the bounded text of `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` when they exist, plus the
names of `README.md`, `STATE.md`, `TODO.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`,
`CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/`. Reads are cached by mtime and size, so a quiet repository costs a
few `stat` calls per turn.

What is left is the part with no other home: environment and tooling traps, the user's own
preferences and corrections, and facts about this machine that the repository cannot know.

Credentials are the one case where a prompt is not enough. `lib/store.js` redacts
credential-shaped strings (`sk-…`, `ghp_…` / `github_pat_…`, `AKIA…`, `xox…`, JWTs, PEM private
keys) at the single write choke point every path goes through, so an auto-capture, a tool call
and a panel paste are all covered. Redaction beats rejection: the sentence around a leaked key
is usually the part worth keeping, so the entry survives with `[redacted]` where the secret was.
The patterns name credential shapes, not "anything that looks random" — a commit id or a sha256
digest is untouched.

Because memory is machine-local, the agent is also told — in the resident recall guidance — to
**promote** an entry that is really a project rule into `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` and then
`memory_forget` it, so the two cannot drift apart.

## Forgetting

Memory that is never read still costs prompt bytes in every injection, so the store does not
only grow. Three things retire an entry, and none of them deletes text — a retired entry keeps
its id, its text and its history, and simply stops being recalled:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `superseded` / `merged` | A newer statement on the same subject replaced it, or a duplicate folded into it. Carries a `supersededBy` pointer. |
| `forgotten` | Someone retired it on purpose (`memory_forget`, or the panel's Forget). |
| `decayed` | Nothing read it for `decayAfterDays` and it is past `decayGraceDays` of age. |

Decay refuses to touch the two kinds whose value is not a function of readership: decisional
entries (including `open`), because a prohibition nobody has tripped yet is still binding, and
`reference` entries, because they are consulted rarely by nature. "Read" means `lastRecalledAt`
when the entry has been read, else its own age. Set `decayAfterDays: 0` to turn decay off.

## Measuring recall

The plugin records what memory is *used*, not only what it stores: `memory_detail`
marks the entry it opened (`recallCount`, `lastRecalledAt`), the panel shows that
count per entry and the store-wide total in its header, and an entry that was
just read counts as fresh when the index is ordered — being used is not punished
by age.

`npm run audit:recall` reads DSH's own session logs (the plugin records no recall
events) and reports what actually happened: which memory tools the agent reached
for, how many entries it opened in full, how often the index had to hide entries,
and which entries are hidden right now. It is read-only, and it decodes a session
log frame by frame, because DSH writes one zstd frame per record.

A run over the first ~7 hours of real use:

```text
tool calls     memory_add=16  memory_detail=13  memory_forget=10  memory_stats=4
               memory_search=0  memory_curate=0
readership     9 of 55 active entries ever opened in full
index          166 injections, 26% of them had to hide entries
eviction       13 of 52 visible entries hidden — 5 decisional, 6 of them read
```

That measurement drove two decisions: the index is now layered (rules and
decisions first, then the most recent facts) because a purely newest-first index
let fresh task narration evict the platform knowledge that had actually been
read, including a live prohibition; and the footer now names `memory_search`
instead of only counting what was withheld.

**Subagents get the tools but not the resident index.** DSH marks a delegated

plugins.description: Per-conversation timestamp toggle for the dsh Web composer: each submitted message is followed by a hidden context message carrying the current local time.
plugins.readme_text:
# @local/dsh-send-timestamp

在 dsh Web 客户端的聊天输入框工具栏右侧加一个「时间戳」开关。开启后，你提交的每条消息后面会跟一条**只带时间戳的隐藏消息**：对话界面里看不到它，但会话记录里存着、送交模型时也在。

```
对话界面：  你： 帮我看下这个报错

会话记录与模型收到：
  你： 帮我看下这个报错
  （隐藏）[10-16 10:23:45]
```

## 行为

| 规则 | 取值 |
|---|---|
| 默认格式 | `[MM-DD HH:mm:ss]`（月-日 + 时:分:秒，24 小时制，本地时间，各段补零） |
| 预设 `time` | `[HH:mm:ss]`（纯时间） |
| 预设 `datetime` | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`（带年份，不带方括号） |
| 预设回落 | 非法/缺省的 `preset` 一律归一化为默认的 `monthday` |
| **开关粒度** | **逐会话**。`sessions[sessionId]` 优先；该会话从没被用户动过开关时，回落到全局 `enabled`。⇒ 在一个对话里关掉**不会**影响其他对话 |
| 会话 id 来源 | Host 侧 `agent.session.id`（`Session.id` 取 `header.id`）；Client 侧取自槽位 standard props 的 `sessionId` |
| 开关落盘 | settings 路径写 `sessions` dict（Host 端 `Schema.dict(Schema.boolean())` + `.volatile()`）；兜底路径写 localStorage 的 `dsh-send-timestamp:sessions` JSON 表 |
| 预设粒度 | **全局**（格式偏好，不逐会话） |
| 注入形态 | **不改写用户原文**：时间戳作为一条独立合成消息追加在批次末尾 |
| 是否显示 | **不在对话框显示**。合成消息的 `source.kind !== 'user'`，Chat 侧经 `contextMessage()` 归为 `context` 节点；而 `isVisibleChatNode()` 会隐藏不含 `tool-addition`/`tool-removal` 块的 context 节点。用户气泡里只有原话，模型与持久会话记录里照样有时间 |
| 去重 | 末尾已是**当前预设同格式**的时间戳时不追加 |
| 斜杠命令 | `/` 开头（含前导空白）不追加 |
| 取时间时机 | `agent/pre-step` 回调里 `new Date()`，绝不在模块加载时取 |
| 触发条件 | 仅当这一批消息里存在 `role === 'user' && source.kind === 'user'` 的那条时才注入（纯插件上下文步骤不注入） |
| 消息身份 | 合成消息 `id` 用 `crypto.randomUUID()`，发布前 `deepFreeze`（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand` 的 `brandString` 是编译期空操作，故与官方 `createUserMessage` 等价） |
| 空文本 | 无 text 片段的纯附件消息不追加 |

## 结构

```
package.json      bundle 声明：dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client
cordis.patch.yml  - insert: 一行插件行；id `send-timestamp` 同时是设置命名空间
src/timestamp.ts  纯函数：格式化 / 追加 / 去重 / 斜杠判定（host 与 client 共用）
src/index.ts      host：Config（volatile）+ agent/pre-step 监听
src/client/index.tsx    client：槽位注册 + 按钮组件
src/client/toggle.ts    开关持久化的唯一接缝
src/client/styles.ts    主题 token 样式
scripts/build.mjs esbuild 构建
test/             node --test 单元测试与冒烟测试
lib/              构建产物（index.js / client.js / timestamp.js）
```

## 构建与测试

```bash
npm install
npm run build      # → lib/index.js、lib/timestamp.js、lib/client.js
npm test           # → node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

构建产物形态：

- `lib/index.js`：ESM，`platform: node`，`@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 保持 external（profile 内已存在）。
- `lib/client.js`：esbuild 的 CJS 产物（`external: ['react']`，classic JSX）包进官方 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: '<npm 包名>', factory })` 外壳。
- `lib/timestamp.js`：纯函数层的独立 ESM 产物，供测试直接 import。

## 持久化

开关与预设走 **dsh 插件设置（profile 配置）**：Host 端 `Config` 用 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 声明，两个字段都 `.volatile()`——设置子系统只把 volatile 字段投影成条目表单，没有 volatile 字段的条目会被 `describe()` 整体跳过。Client 端通过 `ctx.configForms.get('send-timestamp')` 读取与写入（`entryId` 就是 `cordis.patch.yml` 里那一行的 `id`）。

`src/client/toggle.ts` 是唯一接缝：优先 `configForms`，其次第三方 `settingsScope`（`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings` 的兼容面），都不可用时退回 `localStorage`（键 `dsh-send-timestamp:enabled` / `dsh-send-timestamp:preset`）。任何一步失败都只降级、不抛错——组件抛错会让整条槽位条目变空白。

手动改默认值可直接编辑 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`：

```yaml
- id: send-timestamp
  name: '@local/dsh-send-timestamp'
  config: { enabled: true, preset: 'datetime' }
```

## 为什么改写发生在 Host 端

客户端**没有**任何 pre-submit 拦截点：Enter、发送按钮、`inputActions.submit()` 三条入口全部汇入 `SessionInputShell.submit(mode, source)`，且 `inputActions` 只暴露
`captureInsertion` / `insertText` / `setDraft` / `addAttachments` / `removeAttachment` / `pruneAttachments` / `submit` 七个方法，没有 `send` / `steer`。

唯一官方改写点是 `agent/pre-step` waterfall 的 `decision.messages`——它就是即将落库并送交模型的消息数组。改写时必须：

1. 先 `await next()`，并且不拥有决策；
2. `reject` / `signal.aborted` 原样放行；
3. **spread 决策对象**（`{ ...decision, messages }`），否则 `startsRequestSeries` 等字段会丢；
4. 消息对象是深冻结的且新铸了 id，所以只做浅拷贝并替换 `content`：`{ ...structuredClone(m), content }`，保留 `id` / `role` / `source`。

本插件不 import 任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 包（`schemastery` 除外），也不 import `dsh-llm`——那些包不在 profile 的 `node_modules` 里。

## 已知边界

- 时间戳追加在 `decision.messages` 上，而该数组正是随后 `session.append("user/message", ...)` 落库并送交模型的内容，因此落库的与模型看到的都是带时间戳的版本；输入框在**提交后立即清空**，所以界面上不会出现「你输入原文 vs 会话里带时间戳」的分叉。
- 未在真实浏览器里验证的部分：按钮的实际渲染位置与外观、`configForms` 写入是否真能落到 Host 的 profile 文档（依赖运行时服务在场）。
- 设置卡片刻意未实现：官方 `settings.plugin.item` 槽位在 0.2 已删除，现役落点是 `plugins.bundle.config`（key = 包名）或 `settings.plugins.tab`。开关本身就在输入框工具栏里，不需要卡片。
