# dsh-plugin-standards

> DSH 插件开发的**规范与硬约束**合集：UI 组件怎么用、面向 agent 的仓库怎么写、
> 发布前要走哪六步。每条结论都来自本机实测，不是通用道理。

这套文档服务于 `~/Projects/dsh-*` 下的插件仓库。**动手改插件前先读对应那份**，
发布前把 `RELEASE-STANDARDS.md` 的 checklist 逐项过一遍。

## 文档

| 文档 | 管什么 | 何时读 |
|---|---|---|
| [UI-STANDARDS.md](./docs/UI-STANDARDS.md) | 界面必须用 DSH 原生组件；设置页注册在哪；哪些写法会白屏 | 写界面 / 加设置项时 |
| [AGENT-FACING-STANDARDS.md](./docs/AGENT-FACING-STANDARDS.md) | 仓库必须有 `AGENTS.md` + `llms.txt`，README 要指路；各自写什么 | 新建仓库、补文档时 |
| [RELEASE-STANDARDS.md](./docs/RELEASE-STANDARDS.md) | **发布前六步**：文档齐套 → 全面脱敏 → 测试可复现 → 打包核对 → 推前硬闸 → 授权发布 | **发布前逐项执行** |

## 一句话规则（速查）

1. UI 一律用 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`，别自己写组件。
2. 插件设置注册到 `plugins.bundle.config`（key = 包名），不要 `settings.section` / `plugins.item`。
3. 每个公开仓库必须有 `AGENTS.md` + `llms.txt`，README 正文前 1/3 处指路。
4. 发布前脱敏扫**五条**（路径 / 内网 IP / 私人邮箱 / 凭据 / **git 历史**），全部 0 命中。
5. `npm test` 必须一条命令跑完；关键守卫要**变异验证**。
6. `push` / 建仓库 / 发 npm 都要**用户明确授权**。

## 使用方式

本目录通常被工作区软链引用（例如 `~/Projects/dsh-plugin/docs/` → 这里的 `docs/`），
所以在插件仓库里可以直接引用：

```markdown
规范：`docs/RELEASE-STANDARDS.md`（工作区软链）
```

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 blancatora

plugins.description: Aggregate DSH plugin catalogs into a plugin-market index format 1 document for the DeepSeek Harness Discover tab
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-discover-index

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Aggregates the live [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/) catalog into
**plugin market index format 1** — the JSON document the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
(DSH) Discover tab reads.

Published index: <https://hytime.github.io/dsh-discover-index/index.json>

> [!NOTE]
> **Requires a recent DSH, and it is used as a custom market.**
> This index is consumed by the experimental **Custom plugin markets** feature, not by
> DSH core. That feature first shipped in **DSH 0.2.1-alpha.4** (2026-10-15) and is
> carried by every 0.2.1 build since; an older DSH has no Discover tab and no way to add
> an index source. It is still marked experimental upstream, so it is off by default and
> you switch it on yourself — see [Using it in DSH Discover](#using-it-in-dsh-discover).
>
> Nothing here patches or extends DSH: this repository only publishes a JSON file, and
> DSH reads it once you point the feature at that URL.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This project is a conversion and aggregation source, not a security review.**
> Every entry in the index is third-party data republished from upstream. Nothing here
> audits, sandboxes, or endorses the plugins it lists. Installing a DSH plugin runs
> third-party code inside your harness; review the plugin's source before you install it.

## Status

Published and automated. The index URL above serves a live document, rebuilt daily by
[`build.yml`](.github/workflows/build.yml) and deployed only after the real
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index` validator accepts it.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| TypeScript | compiles clean |
| Tests | Pass offline against fixtures recorded from the live catalog — `pnpm test` |
| Published index | Format 1, accepted by the real validator, rebuilt daily |
| Automation | daily cron, plus `workflow_dispatch` for a manual rebuild |

The exact plugin count is deliberately not quoted here: the pipeline reads the live
catalog, so it moves by a few entries between runs as upstream gains, loses, and re-pins
repositories. Query the index, or read the run summary in Actions, for today's number.
See [Running locally](#running-locally) to build it yourself.

## Run your own market

This repository is a template. Fork it, point it at a catalog, and it publishes your own
market at your own GitHub Pages URL, rebuilt daily — no server, and nothing hardcoded to
this account. **[Publishing your own plugin market →](FORKING.md)**

## What it produces

`dist/index.json` — a single format-1 document, published at
<https://hytime.github.io/dsh-discover-index/index.json>. Additional **profiles** declared
in `config/config.yml` each produce their own document (for example a star-floor subset
published as its own market), and each is validated independently in CI.

### What the market declares

Format 1 lets a market publish its own curated vocabulary, and Discover renders all of
it. This market uses each axis:

| Axis | What is declared | What it gives you in Discover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata.categories` | Upstream's 23 categories, translated | The category pills above the list |
| `metadata.labels` | Permission capabilities, risk findings, popularity buckets | The **Labels** filter menu and the tags on each card |
| `metadata.sortKeys` | `stars`, `downloads`, `added` | **Sort** menu entries, each opening descending |
| `metadata.keywords` | Runtime identity, category, and capability words | Free-text search recall |

**Labels** are the most useful of the four, because they answer questions the upstream
catalog cannot. They come from three places:

- **Capabilities** — upstream's trust scan reports what each plugin's code can reach:
  `fs-read`, `fs-write`, `network`, `shell`, `env`, `credentials`, `llm`,
  `host-runtime`, `dynamic-code`, `subagent`. Filtering for `shell` finds every plugin
  that can run commands on your machine.
- **Risk findings**, normalised into five classes rather than the 86 raw sentences
  upstream publishes (most name a single domain or IP): `risk:credentials-and-network`
  (476 entries), `risk:plaintext-http` (97), `risk:literal-ip` (47),
  `risk:install-time-code` (22), and `risk:dynamic-code`.
- **Popularity buckets** — `stars:1k+` / `100+` / `10+` / `1+` / `0` and
  `downloads:10k+` / `1k+` / `100+` / `1+` / `0`.

Popularity is bucketed rather than exact, and that is a format constraint: a label id is
declared once and *referenced* by plugins, so there is no per-plugin label value. Exact
values would need 235 labels for stars and 1,690 for downloads, which turns the filter
menu into an unusable list. The exact numbers are still there where they matter — they
are the `stars` and `downloads` sort keys, and DSH hands them to the model through its
`plugin_market` tool.

### Sources

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Upstream catalog (the data) | <https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json> · [awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) |
| Version history (npm) | <https://registry.npmjs.org/> — one document per npm package |
| This converter (the code) | <https://github.com/hytime/dsh-discover-index> |
| Published index (what DSH reads) | <https://hytime.github.io/dsh-discover-index/index.json> |

The index is a **conversion** of the upstream list, not an independent registry. Upstream
curates and hosts the catalog; this repository only converts it to format 1, checks it
against the real validator, and republishes it on a daily schedule. A bad entry should be
reported upstream; a bad *conversion* of a good entry belongs here.

### Version history

Upstream names exactly one version per entry. DSH's plugin page lists every version it can
install and refuses those the running DSH does not satisfy through `engines.dsh` — neither
of which means anything with a single version per plugin. The build therefore reads each
npm package's registry document and lists every version that declares `dsh.bundle`, is not
deprecated, and has a publish time (2,607 documents, roughly 150 MB on a cold run).

Git-resolved plugins still list the one version their pinned commit declares. A registry
that cannot be reached is not fatal: the plugin keeps its upstream version, because losing
a plugin to a registry outage would be worse than showing one version of it.

### Provenance in the document

The published document carries that provenance in its own `description`, so the source
travels with the data and is visible in Discover without consulting this README:

```json
"description": {
  "en": "The awesome-dsh-plugin list converted to the plugin market index format 1. Source: https://github.com/hytime/dsh-discover-index",
  "zh": "由 awesome-dsh-plugin 列表转换而来的插件市场索引（格式 1）。源码：https://github.com/hytime/dsh-discover-index"
}
```

## How upstream data maps to format 1

Upstream `plugins.json` is a curated list with its own schema; format 1 has a stricter
one. The aggregator converts entry by entry, and the two install paths differ:

| Upstream entry | Format-1 result |
| --- | --- |
| Names an npm package (`npm` + `version`) | One version with `source: { "type": "npm" }`. The package name is authoritative — it is what the registry actually serves — and installation needs no build step on the user's machine. The name is taken from the package, never inferred from the repository name. |
| Git-only (no npm package) | The repository is resolved, its manifest read, and one version emitted with `source: { "type": "git", "url": …, "commit": "<40-hex SHA>" }`. The commit is **pinned**, never a branch or tag, so an index entry always resolves to immutable code. |
| Monorepo subdirectory | The repository and the package directory are split into `repository.directory` (display) and `source.path` (install). |
| Cannot be resolved to a real package name and version | **Dropped.** Format 1 requires a non-empty `versions` array, so an unresolvable entry is never emitted as an empty shell. `node dist/cli.js doctor` reports every drop and why. |

Other mapping rules:

- **Display metadata** — titles, descriptions, icons, author, and repository come from
  upstr

plugins.description: DSH plugin — free OpenCode Zen models for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Free LLM API, no API key needed. 在 DSH 中使用 OpenCode Zen 免费模型，无需 API key
plugins.readme_text:
# opencode2dsh **Free OpenCode Zen models, natively inside DSH (DeepSeek Harness).** No API key. No registration. No extra process. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/blob/master/LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-blue)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh) English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- opencode2dsh registers a native DSH `LlmAdapter` that streams directly from [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen)'s **anonymous free lane** — the same models OpenCode's own CLI uses without an account, served to your DSH model picker as a regular provider called `opencode2dsh`. Requests leave your machine looking exactly like traffic from the OpenCode CLI (same user agent, same correlation headers), and the model catalog stays fresh through a three-tier fallback chain. There is nothing to log into and nothing to host. ## Highlights - **Zero credential, zero setup** — the anonymous lane needs no key; install, restart, chat - **Native adapter, no sidecar** — one npm package, no child process, no binary, no local port (the legacy Go sidecar is not part of the published package; see `legacy/`) - **CLI-identical disguise** — requests carry the OpenCode CLI user agent and its session/request/project header set, derived per conversation - **Selectable thinking levels** — reasoning-capable free models expose an effort picker in DSH's model selector (declared ladders where the model metadata provides them, Off/Minimal/Low/Medium/High otherwise); Responses-only `muse-spark-*` models expose only upstream-supported effort levels, and no selection keeps the provider default - **Image input where it is declared** — image attachments are accepted for every model whose [models.dev](https://models.dev) entry lists `image` in `modalities.input`, and refused for the ones that declare `text` only; models.dev being silent falls back to the live-verified vision family - **Live catalog with a fallback chain** — live upstream list ∩ free-by-metadata, falling back to offline cache and a verified static list - **Self-healing** — fast startup retries, periodic refresh, and a written health snapshot for diagnostics - **Proper error surfaces** — upstream failures (rate limit, auth, timeout, transport) arrive in DSH as classified finish reasons, and retries stay owned by DSH ## Install **From the plugin market** (recommended, once this repo is listed there): in DSH open **Settings → Plugin Market**, search `opencode2dsh`, one-click install. **From npm**: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin ``` **From source** (build the tarball yourself): ```sh git clone https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh.git cd opencode2dsh/packages/plugin pnpm install && pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./opencode2dsh-dsh-plugin-.tgz ``` **Verify**: restart `dsh web`, open the model picker, and pick a model from the **opencode2dsh** group. Requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) 0.1.7 or newer with a web profile (the IP 池 settings page rides the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract); Node.js ≥ 20 (already present if DSH runs); outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` and `models.dev`. ## Configuration Defaults work out of the box. Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: opencode2dsh name: '@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin' config: mode: adapter # adapter (default) | sidecar providerId: opencode2dsh refreshSeconds: 300 # catalog refresh cadence ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `mode` | `adapter` | `adapter`: native LlmAdapter streaming straight from Zen. `sidecar`: legacy local-agent mode, not bundled — build the agent from `legacy/agent` and pass `agentPath`. | | `providerId` | `opencode2dsh` | Provider name shown in DSH. | | `refreshSeconds` | `300` | Live catalog refresh interval. Pricing metadata refreshes every 24 h. | | `agentPath` | auto-resolved | Sidecar only: path to the agent binary. | | `agentArgs` | — | Sidecar only: extra CLI args for the agent. | | `restartDelayMs` / `restartMaxDelayMs` / `maxConsecutiveCrashes` | `1000` / `60000` / `5` | Sidecar only: restart backoff and circuit breaker. | | `firstEventMs` / `bodyIdleMs` / `responsesBodyIdleMs` | `30000` / `120000` / `300000` | Adapter only, plugin 0.3.7+: stream-liveness watchdogs, in ms (integers from `1` to `600000`). Time to the first stream event, mid-response body silence, and the body-idle floor for Responses models (`muse-spark-*`). Increase `firstEventMs` for slow cold starts. Unset keeps the defaults; restart DSH after editing. | ## How it works ``` DSH session │ harness chunks (block-start / text-delta / usage / finish …) ▼ ZenAdapter (registered LlmAdapter) │ pi-ai openai-completions stream (chat models) │ pi-ai openai-responses stream (`muse-spark-*`, Responses-only on Zen) ▼ https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 ← Authorization: Bearer public with CLI-identical headers: user-agent: opencode/… x-opencode-client, x-opencode-session, x-session-affinity, X-Session-Id, x-opencode-request, x-opencode-project ``` - **Session correlation** — session/project ids are SHA-256 derived from the conversation's first user turn (stable per conversation, non-reversible), and each request gets a fresh random id, mirroring the CLI. - **Catalog fallback chain** — S1: live `GET /v1/models`; S2: models.dev pricing metadata decides "free"; S3: a compile-time verified static list. A disk cache (~7-day TTL) covers upstream outages. - **Resilience** — the adapter registers immediately at startup; if the first catalog fetch races your network (VPN/TUN reconnects, DNS), the plugin retries on a short cadence (~1 min) before settling into the periodic refresh. - **Sidecar mode** (`mode: sidecar`, legacy) — spawns a local Go agent (a single-tenant port of [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)) on `127.0.0.1:`, token-authenticated, and registers a standard `llm-pi-ai` route. **Not part of the published package**; build it from `legacy/agent` (`go build ./cmd/agent`) and point `agentPath` at the binary. ## Health & troubleshooting The plugin writes a health snapshot after every refresh round: ``` ~/.opencode2dsh/adapter-status.json ``` ```json { "status": "ready", "total": 64, "exposed": 9, "lastError": "", "writtenAt": "2026-08-29T07:01:54.915Z" } ``` | Symptom | Likely cause & fix | | --- | --- | | `403 FreeTierError` / "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" | The upstream restricts free-tier clients. The plugin preserves the explanation instead of reporting an invalid API key. Use the supported OpenCode client or an official API service. | | Boot screen shows `Failed to load plugins … list slot "plugins.item" requires options.id`, or the IP 池 entry has no configuration page | Your DSH predates the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract. Upgrade DSH to 0.1.7 (latest recommended). On 0.1.6 and older the page never mounts (it is gated on `configForms.whileServed`) — model routing is unaffected. | | DSH 0.1.7/0.2 cannot start after plugin installation (`pending … settingsScope`) | Upgrade the plugin to 0.3.5. On DSH 0.2, configure IP pooling through the installed opencode2dsh row on the Plugins page. | | Only 3 models | Startup fetch raced your network; retries land within ~1 min. Check `adapter-status.json` for `lastError`. | | `lastError: "fetch failed"` persisting | Outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` blocked; check proxy/VPN rules. | | Rate-limit errors in chat (`429 … Endpoint is unavailable`) | The anonymous lane is quota-per-IP and free models are contended. Since the fix for [#51](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/issues/51) the plugin's provider retry policy rides out 429 bursts silently (8 retries, ~1s→20s backoff, ≈90s worst case per step) instead of sur

plugins.description: DSH 代理中心：独立 mihomo 内核、订阅节点、全局 TUN、系统代理与多跳链式代理。
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH 代理中心

DSH 内的独立 mihomo 客户端。

0.3.1 的下载校验、依赖来源及 Windows 验证范围见 [审查证据](docs/AUDIT-EVIDENCE.md)。商城复核尚待固定新提交和补齐文档中的验收项。

[English](README.en.md) · Windows x64 · DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 · Node.js ≥ 22.19

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-tun-proxy?label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tun-proxy)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-tun-proxy)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tun-proxy)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-%E2%9C%93-2ea44f)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64-0078D6)](#安装)
[![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522.19-339933)](package.json)

- 多订阅：导入、切换、更新、流量配额、定时更新、编辑。
- 代理：策略组、节点选择、搜索、排序、批量测速。
- 连接：实时速率、流量趋势、连接列表、单独/全部断开。
- 规则：运行规则、自定义前置规则。
- 链式：2–8 跳 TCP 代理。
- 系统：TUN、Windows 系统代理、DNS、IPv6、自动启动、关 DSH 时自动停代理（可选）。
- 维护：日志、内核更新、本地备份与恢复。
- 检测：一键查询当前出口 IP、地区与所属节点（经本机混合端口发出，反映真实出口）。
- 界面：继承 DSH 主题及玻璃配色。

## 安装

~~~powershell
git clone https://github.com/scclovez/dsh-tun-proxy.git
cd dsh-tun-proxy
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/install.ps1
~~~

重启 DSH，在左侧打开“代理中心”。TUN 需要管理员权限。

面板“概览 → 连接”里的 **“关 DSH 时关代理”** 开关（设置项 `stopOnExit`，默认关闭）：打开后，正常退出 DSH 或停用本插件时会停止内核并尝试恢复系统代理。强杀 DSH 无法触发退出钩子，内核可能继续在后台运行；可用面板或 `node scripts/cli.mjs stop` 停止本插件所属内核。

## 测试

~~~powershell
$env:DSH_TEST_KERNEL = 'C:\path\to\mihomo.exe'
node --test
node scripts/acceptance-tun.mjs
~~~

默认混合端口 17890。状态保存在 %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\tun-proxy。

参考 [FlClash](https://github.com/chen08209/FlClash) 的功能组织（03f9553，GPL-3.0，仅功能参考，未包含其代码），插件代码独立实现。

## 许可证

本项目**自身代码**使用 [MIT](LICENSE) 协议，版权归 [scclovez](https://github.com/scclovez) 所有。

本包**不分发任何第三方二进制**：mihomo 内核（GPL-3.0）与 Wintun `wintun.dll`（WireGuard LLC
预编译二进制许可）都由 `tun_proxy_install` 在运行时下载到用户自己的 `%DSH_HOME%\tun-proxy`。
各自协议、义务与维护者注意事项见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

plugins.description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that auto-summarizes a Bilibili video when you send nothing but its link
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-bilibili-video-summary

给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（DSH）用的插件：
**在对话里只发一条 B 站视频链接、不提任何要求时，自动开始总结这个视频。**

不是把链接丢给模型让它猜，而是先把视频变成可总结的素材——逐段时间轴转写稿 + 关键帧拼图——
再按一套固定的方法论产出总结。画面和文字互相校正，避免语音识别把人名、型号、数字说错。

## 装上之后是什么体验

> 你：`https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1xx411c7mD/`
>
> 助手：（自动取素材、读拼图通读画面、回读关键帧核对参数）→ 直接给出一份结论先行的中文总结。

用户明确说了要干什么时（例如「总结这个」「讲了什么」「帮我翻译」），按用户的说法来，
插件不会抢着注入自己的流程。

## 它解决的问题

直接把视频链接给大模型，通常只能得到三种结果：复述标题、复述简介、或者编。原因是模型拿不到视频内容。
这个插件补上两样东西：

1. **转写稿**——优先用 UP 主自己上传的字幕；没有的话用语音识别，带时间轴，可回查原话。
2. **画面**——按固定间隔抽关键帧，再拼成 16 格「接触印相纸」。一份 20 分钟的视频，
   逐张读图要 190 次以上，读拼图只要 12 次左右，全片结构一眼看完，具体参数再回读单帧核对。

## 安装

需要先有 DSH。本插件按 DSH bundle 规范打包，装完即用：

```bash
# 从 npm 安装（发布后）
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-bilibili-video-summary

# 本地开发：直接指向本目录
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/绝对路径/dsh-bilibili-video-summary
```

装好后重启 DSH，插件会同时注册一个工具（`video_material`）和一个 skill（`bilibili-video-summary`）。

## 外部依赖

视频下载和转码依赖两个命令行工具，**插件会自己找，找不到时会给出安装提示**：

| 依赖 | 用途 | 缺失影响 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) | 下载视频/音频、抓站方字幕 | 完全不可用 |
| [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/)（含 ffprobe） | 抽帧、分离音轨 | 只能拿转写稿，没有画面 |

语音识别（ASR）**不内置**，因为它的体积和平台差异都太大。两种选择：

- **不配置**：插件会先尝试站方字幕。B 站很多 UP 主会上传字幕，够用；没有字幕时就只有画面素材，
  总结会缺少逐字内容。此时插件仍可用，只是能力受限。
- **配置一个**：设置环境变量 `VIDEOSUM_ASR_CMD` 指向任何「音频 → 带时间戳文本」的命令，
  `{audio}` 会被替换成音频文件路径、`{out}` 替换成输出 txt 路径。例如：

  ```bash
  # faster-whisper（需要 pip install faster-whisper）
  VIDEOSUM_ASR_CMD=python -m faster_whisper_cli {audio} --out {out} --language zh
  ```

在 Windows 上，DSH 里跑的命令可能拿不到你交互式 shell 的 PATH。若插件报找不到工具，
用环境变量显式指定即可：

```bash
VIDEOSUM_YTDLP=D:\path\to\yt-dlp.exe
VIDEOSUM_FFMPEG=D:\path\to\ffmpeg.exe
VIDEOSUM_FFPROBE=D:\path\to\ffprobe.exe
```

### 只有 yt_dlp 模块、没有 yt-dlp 可执行文件

如果 yt-dlp 是作为一个 Python 包放在某个目录里（而不是装在解释器的 site-packages），
把它所在目录加进来，插件就会用 `python -m yt_dlp` 调用：

```bash
VIDEOSUM_PYLIBS=D:\path\to\dir-containing-yt_dlp
```

这一点特别值得留意：**文件存在不等于能用**。`yt_dlp` 目录躺在那里但不在
`PYTHONPATH` 里时，`import yt_dlp` 会报 `No module named yt_dlp`。所以插件对每个候选
都真的跑一次 `--version` 验证，`doctor` 报出来的版本号就是实测结果。

## 用法

大多数时候不用管——贴链接就行。也可以显式用它：

- **模型侧工具**：`video_material({ action: "probe", url })` 先看是不是目标视频；
  `video_material({ action: "material", url, every: 3 })` 准备全部素材。
- **命令行**（不经过模型，手动跑素材流水线）：

  ```bash
  node lib/video-material.mjs doctor              # 检查 yt-dlp / ffmpeg / ASR 是否就绪
  node lib/video-material.mjs probe    --url <URL>
  node lib/video-material.mjs material --url <URL> --every 3
  ```

### 产物

默认输出到 `./vidsum_out/<视频标题>/`：

| 文件 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `meta.json` | 标题、作者、时长、播放量、简介、章节 |
| `transcript.txt` | `[起-止] 文本` 逐段时间轴转写 |
| `transcript.srt` | 同名 SRT 字幕，可当字幕文件用 |
| `frames/f_*.jpg` | 关键帧单张（默认宽 640） |
| `frames_index.txt` | 单帧 ↔ 时间点对照 |
| `sheets/sheet_*.jpg` | 4×4 关键帧拼图 |
| `sheets_index.txt` | 拼图每格 ↔ 时间点对照 |

### 参数

| 参数 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--every` | 3 | 抽帧间隔秒。演示类调小（1～2），口播访谈调大（5～10） |
| `--width` | 640 | 关键帧宽度。读取耗时主要看像素数，640 宽约为 960 宽的一半，字幕仍可辨认 |
| `--max-frames` | 192 | 上限；视频过长时插件会自动放宽间隔以覆盖全片 |
| `--grid` / `--cell` | 4x4 / 384 | 拼图布局与每格宽度 |
| `--audio-only` | 关 | 只下音频，省流量 |
| `--no-sheets` / `--no-asr` | 关 | 跳过拼图 / 跳过转写 |

## 总结方法论

插件的 skill 里固化了这几条（也是它比「让模型自己看着办」稳定的原因）：

1. **先给一句话结论**，再展开。细节堆太多会把主线埋掉——用户看不懂通常不是因为信息不够。
2. **两遍法读画面**：先读拼图通读全片，再回读关键帧核对具体参数。
3. **语音识别结果不可全信**：型号、人名、数字一律回画面核对；核对不到就标存疑，不假装确定。
4. **静止文档类视频以画面文字为准**，实拍类视频以讲述为准、画面用来确认型号与数据。
5. **不添加视频里没有的信息**，争议内容标明是作者观点；对线类视频说明这是单方面说法。

## 常见故障

| 现象 | 原因 | 处理 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `No module named yt_dlp` | yt-dlp 以 Python 模块形式存在，但不在 `PYTHONPATH` 里 | 设 `VIDEOSUM_PYLIBS` 指向含 `yt_dlp` 的目录 |
| `HTTP Error 412` | 没有 cookies，B 站拒绝 | 放好 `cookies/bilibili.txt` |
| `HTTP Error 567 Unknown Status` | 媒体下载走了**连不上 B 站 CDN 的本地代理** | 见下 |
| `PermissionError` 指向 cookie 文件 | cookie 文件在只读位置，yt-dlp 退出时回写失败 | 插件已自动复制到可写位置；若仍出现，把 cookie 放到可写目录 |

`567` 这个坑最值得说，因为它的报错完全看不出原因。yt-dlp 会读系统代理设置，
如果本机有个代理（例如 `127.0.0.1:7890`）而它连不通 B 站 CDN，每一个媒体分片
都会被判成 `567`；此时 `--simulate` 解析直链是**正常**的，只有真正传数据才失败，
所以很容易误判成限流或权限问题。

插件对 B 站域名自动追加 `NO_PROXY`（`bilibili.com`、`bilivideo.com`、`hdslb.com`、`b23.tv`），
其他站点仍走你原有的代理设置。如果你手动调 yt-dlp 也遇到，加 `--proxy ""` 即可。

## 已知限制

- B 站高画质与部分字幕需要登录。插件会自动读取工作区 `cookies/bilibili.txt`（Netscape 格式）
  或 `--cookies` 指定的文件。Cookie 会过期，过期后请重新导出。
- 转写质量取决于 ASR 引擎与音质；本插件不改善识别本身，只保证错误能被画面校正。
- 只对**用户消息里只有链接**的情况自动触发。如果同时贴了多条链接，只会总结第一条——
  想让插件逐条处理，直说即可。
- 抽帧是等间隔的，不是「智能选帧」。全屏 PPT 或长时间静止画面会有大量重复帧。
- 索引文件（`frames_index.txt`、`sheets_index.txt`）的表头是 **ASCII**，这是刻意的：
  按 GBK 解码中文会把表头变成乱码，而这些索引正是用来看时间点的。

## 开源协议

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

plugins.description: Android companion for DeepSeek Harness | chat, goals, approvals & notifications from your phone, over your LAN. Kotlin + Jetpack Compose.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Mobile — DeepSeek Harness Remote

An open-source Android companion that puts your DeepSeek Harness in your pocket.
Drive sessions, review plans and goals, answer approvals and questions, and get notified when the harness finishes — from your phone, over your network or a relay.

English · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · Français · ไทย

DSH Mobile is an **unofficial companion app** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (MIT). It mirrors the web GUI feature for feature and uses the harness's own visual language. Android only, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose. Its companion on the other end is [**dsh-relay**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay), a harness plugin that adds the authentication layer the harness says it lacks, so this app can reach a harness with a real credential and a pinned key instead of an open port. See [Relay](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Relay). **[dshm.zyphite.com](https://dshm.zyphite.com)** is the project site: what the app is, what it looks like, and how to get it running, on one page. The [**wiki**](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki) is the user-facing guide: [getting started](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Getting-Started), [connecting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Connecting), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Troubleshooting), a [feature tour](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/Feature-Tour) and an [FAQ](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/wiki/FAQ). --- ## Screenshots | Connect | Chat | Trajectory | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | | | | | Recent harnesses with live reachability, LAN discovery, manual `host:port`, auto-connect. | Streamed turns, a glyph per tool, expandable tool cards, permission picker. | The same session as a per-turn ledger with usage totals. | | Session details | Subagents | |:--:|:--:| | | | | Context breakdown, goal, plan mode, background jobs, queued turns, host info, session-log export. | The subagent catalog — open a child's transcript, follow up, or interrupt it. | ## Features - Connecting — finds a harness on your Wi-Fi with an active subnet scan and a readiness handshake, remembers hosts and probes them for liveness on the way in, takes a manual `host:port`, handles loopback for same-device setups, and auto-connects when you tell it to (last used, LAN, or same device). - Navigation — the drawers work like Discord's: swipe right from the left edge for the workspace-grouped chat list, swipe left to close it, swipe left from the right edge for the session details panel. - Chat — streamed turns with reasoning disclosure, markdown, terminal/diff/read/search/web tool cards, a queue dock where you can edit, remove or steer a queued turn, history paging, and multi-photo and file attachments. Drafts are kept per host and session. - Workspace panels — tabbed text, Markdown, image, PDF and isolated HTML previews; native terminal controls with a bundled xterm renderer; archived-session restore in Settings. - Message feedback — confirmed ratings and retraction, with version-conflict handling. - Slash commands and skills — typing `/` lists the session's commands and skills above the composer. The composer checks a `/` line against the session's own command catalog and runs it through the harness's command gateway. Anything the catalog does not claim is sent as a prompt, which is how skills get invoked. With the dsh-rewind plugin on the host, `/rewind` opens a picker. - Everything the GUI does — goals (phases, rounds, pause/resume/edit), plan mode and plan review, permission approvals, user questions, todo dock, subagents (catalog, follow-ups, interrupt), background jobs, workflow runs, skills, model selection, agent presets, session search, trajectory ledger, session export, message feedback. - Notifications — turn complete, goal complete or blocked, review or question waiting for you. A foreground service keeps the connection alive in the background. - Harness look — the exact DeepSeek Harness design tokens (colors, type, radii, disclosure rows, shimmer, ink buttons), with light, dark and system themes. - 11 languages — English, 中文, हिन्दी, Español, Français, العربية, বাংলা, Português, Русский, اردو, ไทย (RTL aware). ### Added in 0.15.0 - A Check now button for updates in Settings > About. The automatic check also runs again when you come back to the app after a few hours. - Workspace links in replies drawn as file and folder pills; a folder opens in Files. - A redesigned Details panel, Workspace screen and Settings, with archived sessions on a tab of their own. ### Added in 0.14.0 - A `/` menu above the composer with the session's commands and skills. - A picker for the dsh-rewind plugin's `/rewind` and `/undo` that asks for confirmation before it restores files. The transcript hides what a rewind withdrew and marks the cut. ### Added in 0.13.0 - Automation catalog, timing edits, delivery history and session shortcuts. - Plugin installation, updates, toggles, removal, progress and recovery. Create plugin stages an unsent draft with the Creator preset when the host offers it. - Timed questions, continued replies, saved answer drafts and reopenable plans. - Draft text and file, folder and session references saved across app restarts. - Model search, YAML document properties and multiline goal editing. - Reverse-proxy path support and tool argument previews while the model is writing. ## Requirements - Android 8.0+ (minSdk 26). - A running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) at `0.2.1-alpha.2`, the protocol baseline for DSH Mobile `0.16.0`. Existing protocol fallbacks remain for `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.1.7-rc.x` and `0.1.6-alpha.x`; new management features need host support. See [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) and the [0.13.0 validation status](docs/VALIDATION-0.13.0.md) for what has been checked on this baseline. ## Quick start 1. Install the latest APK from [Releases](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile/releases/latest). 2. Open the app and choose how to connect. plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: multiple working directories per workspace, like Claude's additional directories / /add-dir
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-folders > A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that gives a workspace **multiple working directories**, like Claude's additional directories: add other folders to a workspace from a composer button or `/add-dir`, and the model can read them and (for read-write folders) edit them with pre-approved sandbox escalation. Works with DSH NEXT, DSH Desktop and `dsh web` on DSH `0.2.1-alpha.5`. 为 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）工作区添加**多个工作目录**的插件，效果类似 Claude 的 additional directories / `/add-dir`：除了工作区本身的目录，还可以把其他目录（例如共享库、文档仓库、另一个前端项目）加入同一个工作区，让模型一起读写。 适配 DSH `0.2.1-alpha.5`（DSH NEXT 2.0.18-next、DSH Desktop Beta）。不修改上游代码，只通过官方扩展点组合：`systemPrompt.context`、`tools/execute`、`approval/request`、`commands`、`connection.fetch`，以及 Web 客户端的 `conversation.input.left` 槽位。 ## 截图 输入框旁的「工作目录」按钮显示额外目录数量： ![输入框旁的工作目录按钮](docs/screenshots/overview.png)

管理额外目录，切换读写 / 只读
直接输入路径，或「选择文件夹…」（桌面端为系统对话框，浏览器中为应用内浏览器）
斜杠命令 `/add-dir`、`/remove-dir`、`/dirs`： ![斜杠命令](docs/screenshots/commands.png) ## 功能 - **输入框旁的「工作目录」按钮**（📁 +N）：点开后可添加、移除目录，切换「读写 / 只读」。保存后从下一轮对话起生效，本工作区的所有会话共享。 - 添加目录有两种方式：在输入框里**直接输入**路径（绝对路径或 `~/路径`，回车或点「添加」），或点「**选择文件夹…**」用选择框挑选。 - 同一个目录不能重复添加：添加时立即检查，写法不同但指向同一目录（末尾斜杠、`/tmp` 与 `/private/tmp`、符号链接、`~/…`）也算重复，会提示「已在列表中」并高亮已有的那一行；已在工作区内、或已是全局目录的路径同样会被拒绝。 - 「选择文件夹…」按环境自动选择：在 DSH NEXT / DSH Desktop 窗口里打开系统文件夹对话框（Finder，与添加工作区相同）；在本机 `dsh web` 中由 Host 打开系统对话框；在局域网或远程浏览器中显示应用内文件夹浏览器（从工作区所在目录开始，可点路径跳转、显示隐藏文件夹）。 - **斜杠命令**（任何有命令入口的界面都可用）： - `/add-dir <路径> [--read-only]` — 添加目录，支持绝对路径、`~/路径`、相对当前工作目录的路径；目录已在列表中时报错（要改读写权限请先 `/remove-dir`） - `/remove-dir <路径>` — 移除目录 - `/dirs` — 列出当前工作区的全部目录 - **模型可见**：每次请求的运行时上下文（紧跟沙箱策略之后）会列出额外目录及其读写权限；该上下文会写入会话日志，回放时可还原。 - **写入权限**：在默认的 `workspace-write` 沙箱模式下，DSH 只允许修改工作区目录本身。对于标记为「读写」的额外目录，模型使用 `write` / `edit` 工具写入时，插件会自动批准这次沙箱提权（审批记录照常写入会话日志 `approval/asked` / `approval/decided`）。 - 「只读」目录不会自动批准，写入仍会询问你。 - 终端命令（bash）写入额外目录仍走正常的提权确认，因为插件无法可靠判断命令会写哪里。 - 会话处于「只读」模式时不会自动批准任何写入；处于「完全访问」模式时本来就不受限制。 - **全局目录**：可在配置里指定对所有工作区生效的目录。 - **读取额外目录的指令文件**（可选，默认关闭）：开启 `loadInstructions` 后，每个额外目录根部的 `AGENTS.md`（没有时用 `CLAUDE.md`）会作为第二段运行时上下文（紧跟目录列表之后）发给模型，类似 Claude Code 的 `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD`。 ## 安装 ### DSH NEXT / DSH Desktop 在应用中打开 **DSH 终端**（托盘菜单或设置顶部的终端入口），执行： ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Fleey/dsh-workspace-folders ``` 然后完全重启应用（托盘 → **退出并重启**，或设置顶部菜单 → **重启应用**）。输入框工具栏会出现文件夹按钮。 建议固定到某个 commit，避免之后的推送悄悄改变运行的代码：`github:Fleey/dsh-workspace-folders#`。 卸载：`dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-workspace-folders`，然后重启。 ### 普通 `dsh web` ```bash dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add github:Fleey/dsh-workspace-folders ``` ### 从本地源码安装（开发用） ```bash git clone https://github.com/Fleey/dsh-workspace-folders.git cd dsh-workspace-folders && npm install && npm run build dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:"$PWD" ``` 仓库中已包含构建好的 `lib/`，因此从 GitHub 安装不需要运行构建脚本，也不需要在 profile 中授权 `allowBuilds`。 ## 配置 默认配置见 [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml)。要修改，在 profile 自己的 `cordis.patch.yml`（例如 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`）里覆盖这一行，注意要写全保留的键： ```yaml - id: workspace-folders config: autoApproveWrites: true # 设为 false 则读写目录的每次写入都需要确认 globalDirectories: # 对所有工作区生效，~ 会展开为主目录 - { path: ~/notes, access: read-only } # storeFile: /absolute/path.json # 默认 $DSH_HOME/workspace-folders.json loadInstructions: false # 设为 true 则把各额外目录根部的 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md 发给模型 maxInstructionBytes: 32768 # 指令上下文整体（含说明与标题）的 UTF-8 字节上限 ``` 配置写错（未知键、非绝对路径、非法 access、`maxInstructionBytes` 不是整数或小于截断标记的长度）会在加载时直接报错，而不是被静默忽略。 ### 额外目录的指令文件（`loadInstructions`） - 只看每个额外目录**根部**：优先 `AGENTS.md`；没有可用的 `AGENTS.md` 时才读 `CLAUDE.md`，两者不会同时读取。空白的 `AGENTS.md` 也算「有」，此时不再读 `CLAUDE.md`。 - 读写目录和只读目录都会读取；目录当前不存在、或没有指令文件时直接跳过，不报错。 - 指向目录外部的符号链接（文件本身或其所在路径）一律视为不存在，不会读取；指向目录内部的链接正常读取。非普通文件（目录、FIFO 等）也会跳过。 - 每次组装请求时同步重新读取，所以修改指令文件后从下一次请求起生效；内容变化时会生成新的运行时上下文快照，并像目录列表一样写入会话日志。 - 整段上下文（开头说明、每个目录的标题、正文）合计不超过 `maxInstructionBytes` 字节；超出时在 UTF-8 字符边界处截断，并以 `[Additional-directory instructions truncated here to fit the configured size limit.]` 结尾，后面的目录不再出现。 - 该上下文和目录列表一样是必需上下文（`required`），即使 profile 关闭了可选运行时上下文（`systemPrompt` 的 `includeRuntimeContext: false`）也会保留。 ## 数据存储 目录列表按工作区路径保存在 `$DSH_HOME/workspace-folders.json`（默认 `~/.dsh/workspace-folders.json`）： ```json { "version": 1, "workspaces": { "/path/to/project": { "directories": [ { "path": "/path/to/shared-lib", "access": "read-write" }, { "path": "/path/to/docs", "access": "read-only" } ] } } } ``` 文件可以手动编辑（改完需重启）。如果文件损坏，插件会拒绝加载并在日志中指出文件路径，而不会用空列表覆盖它。 ## 限制 - 额外目录按**工作区**生效（以会话创建时的工作区目录为准），不是单个会话。 - `@` 文件引用补全、技能发现仍只看工作区目录本身；需要时请让模型用绝对路径访问额外目录。 - DSH 自带的 AGENTS.md 读取只看工作区目录。额外目录的指令文件需开启 `loadInstructions`，且只读取额外目录根部的一个文件：子目录中的 `AGENTS.md`、以及 `AGENTS.local.md` / `CLAUDE.local.md` 本地覆盖文件都不会读取；内容放在运行时上下文中，不会像工作区指令那样按目录逐级合并。 - 如果某个额外目录恰好是工作区的上级目录（例如项目根），DSH 自身可能已经读取了它的 `AGENTS.md`，开启 `loadInstructions` 后同一内容会出现两次。 - 只有 `write` / `edit` 工具的写入会被自动批准；终端命令写入需要确认。 - 没有挂载任何目录选择器的组合里不会显示「选择文件夹…」，此时直接输入路径即可。 - 在还没有发送过消息的新会话里执行 `/dirs` 等命令，结果不会显示在空白首页上（命令已执行并记录在会话日志中）；用输入框旁的按钮查看更直观。 ## 开发 ```bash npm run typecheck # TypeScript 检查 npm test # 单元测试（vitest） npm run build # 生成 lib/index.js（Host）与 lib/client.js（Web 客户端） npm run check # 以上三项 ``` `lib/` 会被提交到仓库（供 `github:` 安装直接使用），修改源码后请运行 `npm run check` 并一起提交 `lib/`。 端到端冒烟测试：用真实的 `dsh --profile headless` 和 DSH 自带的 LLM mock（无需 API key），在临时 `DSH_HOME` 中验证上下文注入、`loadInstructions: true` 时首个模型请求带上额外目录的指令（且默认不带）、读写目录的自动批准、只读目录不批准、以及不装插件时写入被拒绝： ```bash node scripts/smoke-headless.mts /@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js /packages/test-support/llm-mock-server/src/index.ts ``` 需要 Node ≥ 22.19 和 `zstd` 命令行工具。 ### 结构 | 文件 | 作用 | |---|---| | `src/index.ts` | 插件入口：挂载上下文、自动批准、命令、路由（所有 Host 服务均为可选） | | `src/folders.ts` | 生效目录计算、校验、写入授权判断、模型上下文文本 | | `src/instructions.ts` | 读取额外目录根部的 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`，生成有字节上限的指令上下文 | | `src/approval.ts` | 跟踪提权的 `write`/`edit` 调用，应答匹配的审批请求 | | `src/commands.ts` | `/add-dir`、`/remove-dir`、`/dirs` | | `src/routes.ts` | `/api/workspace-folders/{state,save,pick,browse,resolve}` | | `src/store.ts` | JSON 存储（原子写入、按顺序串行） | | `src/client/index.tsx` | 输入框按钮与对话框 | ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

plugins.description: DSH web plugin: a Smart Prompt button under the composer that rewrites your draft into a structured prompt grounded in the project documents you declare (AGENTS.md / README.md), capped at 400 characters, configured entirely by the caller.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-smartprompt

A [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web plugin that adds a **Smart Prompt** button
under the composer. Click it and your rough draft is rewritten into a structured, executable prompt
grounded in your workspace conventions — then filled straight back into the composer.

```
┌─ composer (draft: "make the login form safer") ─┐
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ✨ Smart Prompt          ← appears only while the draft is non-empty
```

- Empty draft → the button is not rendered.
- Click → the button shows *Optimizing…*, the result replaces the draft, the button turns into *✓ Optimized*.
- Failure → one line of explanation next to the button (timeout / no model / model error); the draft is untouched.
- Each click leaves one `command/run` + `command/done` pair in the session log (that is how DSH's command
  channel works). The plugin renders that as a single-line summary in the conversation
  (*✨ Smart Prompt · N chars · Fill composer*), never as the whole prompt.

中文摘要见文末。

## Install

Three routes, in order of availability today:

| Route | Command | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Git (works now) | `plugin_manager(action="install_bundle", target="github:shellpower96/dsh-prompt-optimizer#v0.1.0")` | ✅ published |
| DSH Discover (market index) | add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shellpower96/dsh-prompt-optimizer/main/market/index.json` as an index source | ✅ published |
| npm | `npm i -g dsh-smartprompt` / `install_bundle dsh-smartprompt` | ⏳ name reserved, publish pending |

The package name is **`dsh-smartprompt`** (the npm name `dsh-prompt-optimizer` already belongs to a
different project). The repository keeps its original name, so every git spec stays valid.


DSH's plugin catalog is the package manager itself — there is no separate submission portal.
Install this bundle from its git repository:

```text
plugin_manager(action="install_bundle", target="github:shellpower96/dsh-prompt-optimizer#v0.1.0")
```

...or from a local checkout while developing:

```text
plugin_manager(action="install_bundle", target="/absolute/path/to/dsh-prompt-optimizer")
```

Installing needs `pnpm` on `PATH` (the plugin manager runs `pnpm add`); without it you get
`spawn pnpm ENOENT`. Remove with:

```text
plugin_manager(action="remove_bundle", target="dsh-prompt-optimizer")
```

The Host half registers the command; the Client half ships as a browser module via
`dsh.client`. Installing a new bundle can arrive over HMR — if the button does not appear,
refresh the page once.

## Minimal example

An empty config is enough:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: prompt-optimizer
      name: 'dsh-prompt-optimizer'
      config: {}
```

To point it at your own conventions (this is the only integration surface — the plugin assumes
no project layout):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: prompt-optimizer
      name: 'dsh-prompt-optimizer'
      config:
        docs: ['AGENTS.md', 'README.md', 'docs/architecture.md']
        contextChars: 6000
        systemPromptLocale: auto
```

## Configuration

Every value is read from the row's `config`; the plugin reads no environment variables and no
settings module of its own. Invalid values throw at activation with the field name.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; `false` registers nothing |
| `maxDraftChars` | `4000` | Reject longer drafts instead of sending them to the model |
| `contextChars` | `8000` | Total character budget for the project-facts block |
| `maxOutputChars` | `400` | Character cap for the optimized prompt, defined in Chinese characters; the English ceiling scales to 1.8x. The meta prompt targets 75% of it, so the hard cap only trims a runaway answer |
| `timeoutMs` | `120000` | Per-call timeout |
| `docs` | `["AGENTS.md","README.md"]` | Workspace-relative documents read as facts, in order; missing files are skipped, absolute paths and `..` are rejected |
| `includeGoal` | `true` | Include the session's current goal in the facts block |
| `systemPromptLocale` | `"auto"` | Language of the meta prompt: `auto` follows the draft's script, `zh`/`en` force one. The produced prompt always follows the draft's language |

## How the prompt is produced

The meta prompt pins five properties (`src/prompt.js`):

1. **Faithful** — clarify, complete, structure; never widen or narrow scope. User decisions become `TBD: …`.
2. **Grounded** — modules, files, commands, conventions and test approaches may only be named if they
   actually appear in the facts block; otherwise the model writes *needs locating* instead of inventing them.
3. **Structured** — Goal / Current state and landing spot / Constraints and conventions / Task breakdown /
   Acceptance criteria; empty sections are dropped.
4. **Executable** — acceptance criteria must be verifiable (a command, an observable behavior, a concrete file).
5. **Concise** — one length budget per locale, expressed in that locale's native unit (Chinese characters /
   English words), plus a bullet discipline: at most 3 bullets per section and 10 in total, no background
   preamble, no restating the draft, no duplicated constraints.
6. **Body only** — no preamble, no reasoning, no code fence; `finalizeOptimizedText()` strips a fence or
   preamble the model adds anyway.

### Length budget

With the default `maxOutputChars: 400`:

| Locale | Target written into the meta prompt | Hard ceiling on the result | Token budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| zh | 300 字 | 400 characters | 334 |
| en | 94 words | 720 characters | 600 |

The target sits below the ceiling on purpose, so a compliant answer is never truncated. If a model
overruns anyway, `finalizeOptimizedText()` cuts at the last complete line (falling back to a sentence
end, then a word break, then a hard cut) and appends a single `…` — it never slices mid-sentence and
never writes explanatory text into the prompt body.

## Layout

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host entry: validate config, register `/optimize-prompt` |
| `src/config.js` | Defaults + hand-written validation (fails loudly) |
| `src/facts.js` | Fact collection: read-only, bounded, never throws; branch comes from `.git/HEAD`, no subprocess |
| `src/prompt.js` | Pure: draft parsing, meta-prompt assembly (zh/en), output cleanup |
| `src/optimize.js` | Orchestration: parse → collect → resolve model route → stream → clean |
| `client.js` | Browser half: composer button, command-row renderer, copy |

Model route: the session Agent's own `provider`/`model` wins, then the process default model
selection (`ctx.agentDefaultModel`). The call goes through `ctx.llm.stream()`, so `llm/stream`
middleware still applies.

## Tests

```bash
node --test
```

Three groups: public-API unit tests, **no-project-context instantiation** (no `fs`, no `cwd`,
no `goals`, no default model — assertions are "explicit outcome, never an uncaught throw"), and a
project-context regression that drives the plugin with a caller-declared `docs` list.

## Known limits

- **Only renders once a session exists.** The button lives in `conversation.composer.dock`
  (scope `session`), so a brand-new conversation's first screen has no button; it appears after the
  first message.
- **The command name is fixed** (`optimize-prompt`): both halves build the command line from a
  shared constant, and DSH rejects two registrations of the same name in one scope. Renaming it
  means editing `index.js` and `client.js` together.
- **Not a tool**: the plugin changes no system prompt and adds no agent tool.
- **Length is a soft promise plus one hard cut**: models are asked to stay inside the budget; the cap is
  only a guard rail. Raising `maxOutputChars` raises both the target and the ceiling. Every default in
  `src/prompt.js` derives from this one config value, so they cannot drift apart.
- Verified against **DSH 0.2.0-rc.2**. No `peerDependencies` are declared on purpose: DSH blocks
  installation on an incompatible peer, which would be worse than a documented version note.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

---
